Your Fiverr Answers account

You sign in to Fiverr Answers using your Fiverr login details. Your Fiverr Answers account is separate from your main Fiverr account. Closing or deleting your Fiverr Answers account will not affect your Fiverr account.

When you sign in to Fiverr Answers, you are automatically added to the Fiverr Answers mailing list. Emails from the platform are sent from noreply@invisioncloudcommunity.com.

Some freelancers may find that a Fiverr Answers account was created on their behalf when they were enrolled in the platform. This is expected behavior and does not affect your Fiverr account in any way.

Troubleshooting

If you are experiencing trouble signing in to Fiverr Answers, try the following steps:

  • Make sure you are using the same login credentials as your Fiverr account.
  • Try signing in from a different browser or an incognito window.
  • If the issue continues, contact our Customer Support team for help.

If you are invited but cannot see the option to post answers, make sure you are signed in. If you are signed in and still cannot answer questions, contact our Customer Support team.

If one of your professions is not showing on Fiverr Answers, this may be a technical issue. Contact our Customer Support team and include a screenshot showing the missing profession.

Using Logo Maker as a freelancer (Freelancers: Features & programs)

Logo Maker lets clients purchase a ready-to-use logo built from a design you create, then edit it themselves with no extra work from you. Once a client buys one of your designs, we give them tools to customize it, and you continue earning from that design over time.

Before you begin

This article is for freelancers who already have a Logo Maker account. Logo Maker is currently closed to new freelancers.

There are two levels of access within Logo Maker:

  • All current Logo Maker freelancers can edit, track, and earn from their published designs.
  • Only a limited number of eligible freelancers can add new logos at this time. If you become eligible, we’ll notify you.

If we reopen the program to new freelancers, or expand upload access, we’ll let you know.

To access Logo Maker, log in, switch to selling, and go to My Business > Logo Maker.

How Logo Maker works

Clients can purchase a logo without any extra effort from you. After a client buys your design, they can:

  • Enter their brand name, slogan, design, and branding preferences into Logo Maker’s Brief Wizard. They see a personalized, real-time catalog of logos that best match their brand name and slogan.
  • Edit the logo and adjust typography, colors, and layout using the Editor tool.

There is no communication between you and the client for Logo Maker orders. You cannot make revisions, and you do not influence the client’s design choices.

Customizations & packages

If a client wants specific customization from you, they can order a custom service directly from you.

After a client purchases a logo, they can upgrade the logo package or buy additional logo variations. This generates more revenue for you, since 20% of every additional order goes to you, with no extra effort required.

  • If a client purchased the basic package, they can upgrade to the professional package for $30 USD within the first 72 hours, or for $45 USD after that. Clients can also purchase additional logo variations, such as font, layout, and color, for $15 USD per variation.

Logo statuses

Each logo design you publish has a status:

  • Pending: the logo stays in pending mode for up to four days before it turns active.
  • Draft: the design is unfinished. Finalize publishing to change its status to active.
  • Paused: the design is published but not offered for sale, so clients cannot see it. Your design switches to paused if you reach your limit of active logos.
  • Active: the design is published and offered for sale.

We occasionally review accounts that reach their limit of active logos and notify you if you’re eligible to increase that limit; however, you can’t currently request an increase on your own.

Tracking your performance with the Logo Maker dashboard

The Logo Maker dashboard gives you general and in-depth information about your logos, statistics, and ways to improve as a freelancer.

To access the dashboard, go to My Business > Logo Maker, then select the Overview, My logos, or Insights tab.

  • In the Overview tab, you can view:
    • Your metrics bar (earnings this month, total earnings, completed orders, clicks, favorites, and impressions)
    • Your performance chart, filterable by earnings, orders, clicks, impressions, and time range
    • Your top logos, filterable by impressions, clicks, orders, and earnings
    • Your recent activity, including recent sales and designs added to favorites
    • Your current earnings share and how close you are to the next tier
    • News and tips
  • At the top of the My logos tab, you can view the number of logos in each status: active, pending, paused, drafts, denied, and total.
  • Below the status overview, you can view the metrics table for a detailed breakdown of each logo design’s performance. You can:
    • Switch between a gallery or list display
    • Search and filter by logo name, industry, or status
    • Click a logo to open a side panel showing its performance data, variations, metadata, and recent orders
  • If a client has already purchased a design, you cannot delete it.
  • The metrics table displays detailed stats of each individual logo design:
    • Status: whether the design is pending, draft, paused, or active.
    • Earnings: the total amount you’ve earned from that design so far.
    • Click rate (CR): how often clients who see the design go on to click it.
    • Orders: the number of times that design has been purchased.
    • Clicks: how many times a client clicked the design.
    • Favorites: how many times clients added the design to their favorites.
    • Impressions: how many times the design was shown to a client.
    • Last order: the date of the design’s most recent order.
    • Actions: the options available for that design, including pausing it, sharing it, editing it, viewing it as a client would see it, or deleting it.
  • The Insights tab shows Logo Maker trends, including top searched industries, top converting industries, top picks by industry and tag, and industries with low logo supply.

The earliest date you can view data in the dashboard is January 1, 2022. Activity and metrics from before this date, including “Total” and “all time” data, are not shown.

Earnings tier model

Your earnings share, the percentage of each sale you keep, is based on your total Logo Maker sales over the last 12 months. The higher your sales, the higher your earnings share.

  • Entry-level freelancers start at a 20% earnings share.
  • We recalculate your tier on the first day of every month.
  • Your earnings share applies as a fixed percentage regardless of which package a client purchased.

The tier-based earnings model took effect on March 1, 2023. It applies to Logo Maker packages (Essential, Professional, and Unlimited), package upgrades, and new paid variations ($15 USD each). It does not apply to other products or services you sell outside Logo Maker.

How to use the Logo Maker dashboard

  • Go to My Business.
  • Select Logo Maker.
  • Choose the Overview, My logos, or Insights tab.
  • Check your current earnings tier and share it under the Overview tab.

Best practices for creating logos

This section is relevant for those freelancers who can upload new logos to Logo Maker.

  • Keep logos simple: favor minimal, focused designs over complex ones, and center each logo around one or two emotions.
  • Design for versatility: use single-letter monograms and leave room for both short and long business names.
  • Avoid duplicate uploads: add real variations in color, layout, or font instead of uploading near-identical designs.
  • Build out variations: aim for four to five varied typography, color, and layout options per logo.
  • Cover different layouts: design for both vertical and horizontal formats, such as social media, business cards, and merchandise.
  • Tag accurately: use simple, element-specific tags based on what’s visually in the logo.
  • Pick a specific industry: choose the most specific sub-industry rather than a broad category.
  • Use color palettes thoughtfully: vary hue, saturation, and value across variations, and avoid gradients.
  • Set up typography and layers first: layering is fixed (text, symbol, shape), so arrange and crop your symbol before uploading.
  • Keep your active lineup strong: swap out lower-performing designs for higher-quality ones over time.

FAQs

  • The new tier-based earnings model took effect on March 1, 2023, and it applies to all Logo Maker packages and new paid variations; however, it doesn’t apply to orders outside of Logo Maker.

  • The monthly calculation works the same way, with fewer months to review. We reevaluate your placement on the first day of each month, starting from the month you began selling logos. Once you’ve sold for 12 or more months, we recalculate your placement based on your total sales in the last 12 months.
  • Yes. If your sales decrease, we may downgrade your earnings tier, since we calculate it based on your last 12 months of sales.
  • Uploading a wider variety of high-quality logos, where you’re eligible to do so, increases your chances of matching more clients, which can raise your income potential.
  • Yes. We determine your upload capacity based on your performance and reevaluate it monthly.
  • You can view your tier on the Overview tab of your Logo Maker dashboard.
  • Yes, it applies to logo packages (Essential, Professional, and Unlimited), package upgrades, and new paid variations ($15 USD each). It does not apply to other products or services you sell outside Logo Maker.
  • We recommend four to five variations that differ in color, layout, or typography. This gives clients more options and increases your chances of a sale.
  • The same symbol in a different color, rotation, or font counts as a variation, not a new design. If you reuse a design, add or remove enough elements to make it distinct before publishing it separately.
  • Pick the most specific sub-industry that fits your design, and tag it based on what’s visually in the logo rather than abstract concepts or industry names.
  • The program is currently closed to new freelancers. Only freelancers who joined before can use Logo Maker. If we start accepting new freelancers, we will let you know.

Using the Fiverr mobile app (Freelancers: Features & programs)

The Fiverr mobile app lets you manage your Fiverr account from anywhere. Whether you are a client searching for services or a freelancer tracking orders and earnings, the app gives you access to the most important Fiverr features from your phone.

Before you begin

The app is available on iOS and Android devices. Some features are only available on the PC, including starting the process to become a freelancer, and changing your email address.

Navigating the app

The Fiverr mobile app has five main menus. The content in each menu changes based on whether you are using a client or freelancer account:

  • Inbox
  • Search
  • Manage orders
  • Account

Home

Functionality for clients and freelancers
  • The Home screen gives clients quick access to services, popular categories, and Fiverr updates.
    • Services search: Search for services on Fiverr, select Gigs, and place orders.
    • Most popular services: Browse popular services by category and save categories as your interests in the Interests tab.
    • What’s new on Fiverr: Read recent news and posts from Fiverr.
    • Recently viewed & more: Return to past Gigs and refer friends to Fiverr through Fiverr’s Refer a Friend program.
  • The Home screen gives freelancers a summary of their performance and activity.
    • Level and Success Score: View information about your current level and Success Score.
    • Orders: See the total number of orders you have received.
    • Unique clients: See how many unique clients you have worked with on the platform.
    • Total lifetime earnings: View the total earnings you have made on Fiverr.
    • New briefs: See all new briefs you have matched with and can respond to.
    • Earnings: View detailed information about your earnings.
    • To-dos: See a list of action items, including:
      • Number of unread messages
      • Number of upcoming deliveries
      • Number of revision requests
      • Number of new orders
    • My Gigs: View analytics for your Gigs over the last seven days, including:
      • Number of impressions
      • Clicks
      • Conversion percentage
  • Learn more about briefs and Success Score with the following articles:
    • Personalized offers (Briefs) for freelancers
    • Success Score

Inbox

The Inbox works the same way for both clients and freelancers. You can view all your conversations, reply to messages, and filter your inbox.

Learn more with Using your inbox effectively.

Search

Search is available to both clients and freelancers, allowing you to find services and browse Gigs. If you are a freelancer and use the Search menu, you will be automatically switched to the client profile.

Learn more with Searching freelancers and services on Fiverr: A guide.

Manage orders

The Manage orders menu is available to both clients and freelancers. From here you can:

  • View all your orders.
  • Message the other party about an order.
  • Send or accept a delivery.
  • Request revisions.
  • Access the Resolution Center and send a request.

Learn more with the following articles:

  • The complete guide to your Fiverr order: Statuses and process
  • Managing your orders: A freelancer’s guide to the Fiverr order process
  • Using the Resolution Center

Account

The Account menu includes options for all users, as well as options specific to clients and freelancers.

Shared functionality

The following features are available to both clients and freelancers:

  • Tap the bell icon to view all notifications you have received.
  • Tap your profile picture to set or update it.
  • Refer a friend and receive a reward through Fiverr’s refer-a-friend program via Invite friends.
  • Manage the following preferences:
    • Notifications: Manage your notification settings and choose which types you want to receive.
    • Security: Enable or disable multi-factor authentication, view the devices connected to your account, and disconnect them.
    • Language: Change the app’s language.
    • Appearance: Switch between Light and Dark mode.
    • Currency: Set the currency you want to pay in.
    • Online status: Set your online status to show other users whether you are online or offline.
  • Account info
    • Username and email: View your Fiverr username and the email address linked to your account. Usernames cannot be changed. To change your email address, go to Fiverr on the web.
    • Personal balance: View your Fiverr balance, including:
      • Balance from canceled orders
      • Total balance
      • Fiverr Credits
  • Account management
    • Deactivation and deletion: Deactivate your account or delete it entirely. Note: Once an account is deleted, it cannot be restored.
    • Privacy: Read Fiverr’s Privacy Policy and request to opt out of sharing your information.
    • Logout: Log out of the app.
  • Support
  • Tap Support to open the Fiverr Help Center, where you can browse articles or contact Customer Support.
  • Community and legal
    • Forum: Go to the Fiverr forum to read and post about Fiverr.
    • Blog: Visit the Fiverr blog for helpful information and tips.
    • Community standards: View Fiverr’s Community standards and platform guidelines.
    • Terms of service: Read Fiverr’s Terms of Service.
    • Privacy policy: Read Fiverr’s Privacy Policy.

Using your Fiverr Portfolio

Your Fiverr portfolio helps potential clients understand your skills, experience, and working style. By sharing past projects from Fiverr and outside Fiverr, you can build trust and show clients what to expect when working with you.

Overview

Your portfolio can include two types of content: portfolio projects and reviews with files (Live Portfolio). Both types appear on your profile page, your Gig page, and your profession page, giving clients multiple opportunities to see your work.

  • Portfolio projects are manually added projects. They can include work you completed on Fiverr or work from outside the platform. You create and manage these yourself.
  • Reviews with files (Live Portfolio) are work samples pulled automatically from completed Gig deliveries, when the Live Portfolio feature is enabled on a Gig. These appear in your portfolio tagged as “Made on Fiverr.”

Within your portfolio, projects and review files appear in the following order:

  • The first two projects you selected and pinned
  • The three most recent review files from your deliveries
  • All other manually added projects (up to 18), in the order you choose
  • All delivery files (up to 17), from most recent to oldest

While a portfolio does not guarantee orders, it helps clients better understand your skills and experience, which can increase trust and improve conversion.

Before you begin

  • All freelancers are eligible to add a portfolio.
  • Portfolio editing is only available on desktop. You can view your portfolio on iOS and Android, but you cannot edit it from the app.
  • Each portfolio project must include at least one file and can include up to five files.
  • You can upload between one and 20 portfolio projects to your profile.

Portfolio projects

Portfolio projects let you manually showcase your work, whether it was completed on Fiverr or outside the platform. There is no client approval flow for manually added projects. You are responsible for ensuring you have the right to display the work, especially if it was completed under a confidentiality agreement.

Adding a portfolio project
- Go to your profile by selecting your profile picture from the dropdown menu.
- Scroll to the Portfolio section and click Add projects, then select Create new project.
- Fill in the project details (see fields below).
- Click Continue, then Publish project.
- From your freelancer dashboard, click on your Profile Strength widget.
- From the list in Profile Strength, choose Showcase portfolio.
- Fill in the project details (see fields below).
- Your profile changes are automatically saved.
Project details
  • This is a required field.
  • Choose a clear, descriptive title. Minimum 15 characters, maximum 50 characters. Use the format: [Client or brand name] – [Project focus or type].
  • This is an optional field.
  • Select the most relevant option from the dropdown.
  • This is a required field.
  • Select from the dropdown. Up to six months.
  • This is a required field.
  • Select from the dropdown. Prices are in USD only.
  • This is a required field.
  • Select the month and year.
  • This is a required field.
  • Minimum 120 characters, maximum 1,400 characters. Explain the client’s needs, your approach, and the outcome.
  • This is a required field.
  • Upload one to five files per project. Accepted formats include JPEG, JPG, PNG, GIF, MP4, AVI, PDF. Maximum file size: 50 MB. Recommended image size: 1,280 x 769 pixels (aspect ratio 5:3).
  • You can upload PDFs to showcase writing samples, reports, case studies, or presentations, as long as they meet Fiverr’s content guidelines.

For portfolio videos, the first frame is automatically used as the thumbnail. You cannot change it. To control how it looks, make sure the first frame clearly represents your work.

Editing or removing a portfolio project

You can edit or remove manually added portfolio projects at any time from your profile. Hover over the project to see the Edit and Delete buttons.

  • If you click Edit, you will be taken to the project details page.
  • If you click Delete, you will be asked to confirm the action.
Organizing your portfolio

You can reorganize your projects by clicking the Reorganize button on your portfolio page, then dragging and dropping them into the order you want.

Note that you can only reorder manually added projects. You cannot reorganize the review files.

Live Portfolio

Live Portfolio is a feature that automatically displays review files from your completed Gig deliveries in your portfolio. When a client leaves a public review and approves the display of the delivered work, the file appears in your Gig gallery and in your portfolio alongside the client’s written review.

Live Portfolio shows your most recent 17 eligible files. As new review files are published, older files are removed.

Live Portfolio cannot be disabled for Gigs in the Logo design and Illustration subcategories. These Gigs show “Live Portfolio On” with no checkbox.

Enabling or disabling Live Portfolio

Live Portfolio is enabled by default for each Gig. To change the setting for a specific Gig:

  • Go to My Business and click on Gigs.
  • In the Gig list, click the dropdown next to the Gig you want to update.
  • Next to Live portfolio, check the box to enable it or uncheck it to disable it.

If you disable Live Portfolio and then enable it again, it will only apply to deliveries made after you re-enable it. Files from orders delivered while it was disabled will not appear.

File eligibility

You can choose which delivery file appears in your Live Portfolio by selecting the file in the delivery message. Once you deliver the order, you cannot change the file that will appear in the review.

For a file to appear in your Live Portfolio, it must meet the following requirements:

  • Accepted file types include PDF, audio files (AAC, MP3, WAV, OGG, and others), video files (MP4, MPEG, WebM, and others), and image files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP, and others).
  • Files delivered in compressed folders, through third-party file-sharing services such as Dropbox or WeTransfer, or as source files will not be included.
How client approval works

Clients can choose whether to allow their delivered work to appear alongside their review. This is their decision and cannot be controlled by you.

If a client wants to remove the delivered work from their review after it has been published, they can do so at any time. Once a file is removed from a review, the action cannot be undone. There is no time limit for clients to remove a file.

For a client to remove the file:

  • Go to the order page and scroll to the review section.
  • Click the ellipsis menu.
  • Click Remove files from review.
  • Confirm the action.

Client approval to share a delivered file does not guarantee its inclusion in the Gig Gallery and Live Portfolio. Fiverr may choose not to display content that does not meet its policies or legal requirements.

Best practices

Use these tips to get the most out of your portfolio.

  • Use the following structure to give clients useful context:
  • Goals: Describe what the client needed to achieve.
  • Challenges: Explain the key obstacles or constraints involved.
  • Solutions: Describe your approach and the tools or methods you used.
  • Outcome: Share measurable results where possible.
  • Focus on quality over quantity. A focused, well-curated portfolio is more effective than a large collection of unrelated work.
  • Update your portfolio regularly as you complete new projects.
  • Remove outdated or less polished work over time.
  • Show variety across different styles, industries, or project types where relevant.
  • You may include client names or logos only if you have their permission. If not, use general descriptions such as “E-commerce brand” or “SaaS startup.”
  • Do not upload projects that include confidential or personally identifiable information, such as taxpayer ID, Social Security number, or credit card number. Always remove or anonymize any restricted data before adding files.
  • If your work cannot be shared publicly due to copyrights, you can share personal projects you have completed and use approximate pricing and timeframes.

FAQs

  • Portfolio projects are visible to clients in three places:
    • Your profile page, scrolling past your Gigs.
    • Your profession page, scrolling past your Gigs.
    • Your Gig page, scrolling past your description.
  • Yes. Portfolio projects can include work from Fiverr or from outside the platform.
  • Yes. You can edit or remove manually added portfolio projects at any time from your profile. Hover over the project to see the Edit and Delete options.
  • Yes, by selecting the file in the delivery message. Once the order is delivered, you cannot change the file.
  • Yes. You can upload PDFs to showcase writing samples, reports, case studies, or presentations, as long as they meet Fiverr’s content guidelines.
  • Yes. Clients can remove the delivered work from their review at any time by clicking the ellipsis menu on the order page review section and selecting Remove files from review. Once removed, the file is also removed from your portfolio and cannot be restored.
  • You must have the client’s explicit permission to use delivered work as a work sample on other platforms.
  • Possible reasons include: the file type is not supported, the file was delivered in a compressed folder or through a third-party service, the client did not approve the file display, or your Gig is in a category where review files are not supported, such as Legal Consulting, Accounting, or Tax Consulting.
  • Do not upload projects that include confidential, private, or sensitive information. Always remove or anonymize any restricted data before adding files to your portfolio.

Your personal Success Manager

As a Seller Plus Premium member, you get access to a personal Success Manager. This expert will provide tips and guidance to help you convert business opportunities into successful orders and grow your business on Fiverr. They offer expert-level advice on everything from Profile and Gig optimization to market best practices.

Overview

  • What is the role of my Success manager? Your Success Manager is a Fiverr expert who shares advice and guidance based on their deep platform knowledge and the best practices of the most successful freelancers. They are here to assist you with key areas of your business.
  • Who is eligible? You must be a Seller Plus Premium subscriber to have a personal Success Manager.
  • How do I sign up? Join Seller Plus Premium here.

Discover how your Success Manager can assist you

Your Success Manager provides support in several critical areas to help you thrive on the marketplace.

  • They will share tips to improve your communication with clients, guidance on Gig keywords, and tricks to boost your Gig’s visibility and conversion. They also guide you on how to handle an active dispute and can help accelerate the response speed of any Customer Support tickets you open.
  • Your Success Manager will guide you through optimizing, restyling, and rethinking your Gig. They use their experience to teach you the best practices for high-level achievement.
  • You can learn how to maximize every feature and benefit by working with your Success Manager. They’ll help you learn how to give top-notch service and increase your chances to qualify for growth programs.
  • Your Success Manager cannot directly promote or demote your seller level. However, they will help you understand how Fiverr works, assist you in climbing the levels ladder, and help prevent future level demotions.

Communicating with your Success Manager

You can leverage your Success Manager’s expertise to get the most out of your Seller Plus Premium subscription.

  • Be proactive: Use your dedicated time to discuss specific goals, such as improving a low-converting Gig or targeting a new client segment.
  • Keep communication clear: When asking for help with a Customer Support ticket, provide the ticket number and a brief summary of the issue to your Success Manager to help them follow up efficiently.
  • Focus on growth: Work with your manager to create a strategy for qualifying for high-performance programs, which can be a key driver of your business growth.

FAQs

  • Your Success Manager cannot directly promote or demote your seller level. However, they are experts on the Fiverr leveling system and will provide you with the advice, best practices, and guidance you need to increase your chances of meeting the requirements for the next level.
  • No, your Success Manager does not replace Customer Support. You must still open a ticket for platform issues. However, one of their roles is to help accelerate the response time on any Customer Support tickets you have already opened.
  • No, access to a personal Success Manager is an exclusive benefit for Seller Plus Premium subscribers only.
  • The guidance and advice your Success Manager provides are customized for your specific business and Gigs. You are free to apply the best practices you learn, but remember that success strategies vary for every seller on the marketplace.
  • You can contact your Success Manager with a personal call or via e-mail. Schedule a call here.

Freelancers: Order management

Best practices for client management

How you respond to a potential client’s first message often determines whether they place an order with you or move on. Responding promptly and professionally shows clients that you are reliable, easy to work with, and invested in their success before the order even begins. This article covers the key practices for handling inbox messages well.

Respond promptly

Reply to new messages as quickly as you can. Clients often reach out to multiple freelancers at once, and a fast response can be the deciding factor. It also directly affects your response rate, which influences your freelancer level eligibility.

If you are not available to give a full reply right away, an auto reply lets clients know you have received their message and will get back to them. Set one up in your inbox settings so clients are never left wondering.

Your response rate tracks how often you reply to first messages within 24 hours. Missing a first message, including messages you suspect are spam, counts against your rate.

Personalize your reply

Generic replies feel like templates and rarely convert to orders. Take a moment to acknowledge what the client has asked for specifically, and tailor your response to their situation. Even a small personal detail, referencing the project they described, or showing that you understand their goal, makes a significant difference.

A useful test: read your reply out loud and ask yourself whether it is an answer you would want to receive. If it sounds generic or unhelpful, revise it before sending.

Be genuinely helpful

Whether you offer advice, a recommendation, or just a clear explanation of what you can do, giving clients what they actually need builds trust and creates a strong foundation for the working relationship. You do not need to do work for free to be helpful. Clarity, expertise, and a direct answer are often all a client needs to feel confident placing an order with you.

End your message with a question

Ending your reply with a relevant question keeps the conversation moving and shows the client that you are engaged. It also helps you gather the information you need before creating an order. Good questions might clarify the scope of work, set expectations early, clarify the client’s deadline, or define the specific outcome they are aiming for.

If you have enough information to make an offer, skip the question and send a custom offer instead. A custom offer shows exactly what you will deliver, at what price, and by when, which makes it easy for the client to say yes.

When to send a custom offer

Once you have a clear picture of what the client needs, a custom offer is often the most effective next step. It removes ambiguity, sets clear expectations, and gives the client a concrete way to move forward. You can create a custom offer directly from the inbox conversation.

Tools to help you stay on top of messages

  • Auto reply: Set up an automatic first response so clients receive an acknowledgement immediately, even when you’re not available.
  • Quick responses: Create saved reply templates for common questions and scenarios, so you can respond faster without sacrificing quality.
  • Availability settings: Set your working hours so clients know when to expect a response. This is especially useful if you work across time zones.

What not to do

  • Do not share personal contact information (email, phone number, social media handles) in your messages. All communication must stay on Fiverr. This is a Terms of Service requirement.
  • Do not ignore messages, even ones that appear to be spam. Report spam promptly, or send a brief reply, to protect your response rate.
  • Do not send the same generic message to every client. Personalized replies convert better and build stronger relationships.
  • Do not make promises you cannot keep. Setting realistic expectations from the first message leads to better reviews and fewer disputes.

Blocking a user from messaging you (Freelancers: Order management)

If you want to stop receiving messages from a specific user on Fiverr, you can block them directly from your inbox. Blocking prevents the user from contacting you and limits their ability to place new orders or send offers. Both freelancers and clients can block users, and you can unblock anyone at any time.

What blocking does

When you block a user on Fiverr, the following restrictions apply:

  • They cannot send you messages.
  • They cannot place new orders with you (if you are a freelancer).
  • They cannot send you offers (if you are a client).

You can unblock a user at any time by going to the same blocking feature and clicking Unblock.

You can only block users you have had a prior interaction with, such as a message exchange before or after an order.

How to block a user from your inbox

- In your inbox, hover over a message from the user you want to block.
- Click the action ellipsis (...).
- Click Report.
- Select a reason for the report.
- Select the option to block the user.
- Open your inbox.
- Long-tap on a message from the user you want to block.
- Tap Report Spam.
- The user is automatically blocked.

Reporting a message & marking spam

From the same action ellipsis (…) menu, you can also:

  • Report: flags the message for a policy violation. You will be asked to select a reason. You also have the option to block the user.
  • Mark as spam: moves the message to your Spam folder.

To report any behavior that violates Fiverr’s Community Standards, see Reporting content or behavior on Fiverr.

What to do when you have an active order

If you encounter an issue with another user while an order is ongoing, contact Fiverr Customer Support immediately for assistance. Once the order is completed, you can block the user from your inbox.

FAQs

  • If you encounter an issue with another user while an order is active, contact Fiverr Customer Support immediately for assistance. You can block the user once the order is completed.
  • After you block a client, they cannot place new orders with you.
  • After you block a freelancer, they cannot send you offers.

Collaboration tool: Communicating on an active order

In order to discuss file content faster and more efficiently, both clients and freelancers can leave comments on image, audio, and video files. Audio and/or video files can be time-stamped, so that all participants know the exact part being referred to.

Use the collaboration tool to easily review files within an active order.

Reading and responding to file comments

  • In an active order, a freelancer can attach a file in the conversation (with a client).
  • Both clients and freelancers can copy and paste the file link into any preferred collaboration tool.
  • A client can open the file and send it back with comments for specific points in the file.
  • When a freelancer gets a message from a client, they can click on it to open the file.
  • On the right-hand side, clients and freelancers can see the various comments.
  • Click the comment to view the details, including the time stamp.
  • Write your replies and click “Submit all comments.”

Note: You can upload files up to 5GB.

Inviting third parties to comment on files

Clients can ask other people (Fiverr users or not) to view and comment on the files sent by a freelancer. Collaboration works the same way as described above but a freelancer won’t see the third party’s comments—only the client can see them.

To invite someone to collaborate on your order files:

  • Click “Share” and add an email address.
  • They will then get an invite.
  • After, you can start notating the files.

Creating and managing custom offers

Custom offers let you proactively propose personalized services and unique pricing to potential clients, helping you grow your business.

Feature functionality

Custom offers are a tool for freelancers to provide tailored solutions that may not be covered by standard Gigs. They help you build trust, adapt to specific client needs, and increase your conversion rate by offering a professional, transparent approach to handling a variety of project types.

Custom offers can be sent through your inbox on the desktop site or the mobile app. Once a client accepts your offer, the order starts automatically.

  • All freelancers with an active Gig can send custom offers.
  • Milestone and subscription custom offers are only available in specific categories.
  • Clients cannot accept a custom offer if your status is set to Unavailable.

Ensure you have no pending offers before setting your account status to Unavailable, as clients can still pay for pending custom offers while you are away.

Learn more with Setting Availability for freelancers.

Pricing and delivery limits

The following standards apply to all custom offers:

  • Minimum of $5 USD up to a maximum of $20,000 USD.
  • Between 0 and 20, or Unlimited.
  • 1 day to 90 days.

Custom offer types

You can choose from four order types based on the project requirements:

Order type

Best use case

Key details

Single payment

Simple tasks completed in one step.

One-time delivery and payment.

Subscriptions

Repeat business and long-term work.

Recur daily, weekly, or monthly for up to six months.

Milestones

Complex projects with multiple phases.

Up to five steps; get paid as you complete each task.

Hourly

Flexible work based on time spent.

Set an hourly rate and a weekly hour limit.

How to create a custom offer

- Log in and go to your messages.
- Click See All in Inbox.
- Select the conversation with the client and click Create an offer.
- Select the Gig you want to offer and choose the order type (Single payment, Subscriptions, Milestones).
- Select a package to auto-populate details or customize the fields manually.
- Optional: Add an expiry date and the number of revisions.
- Click Send offer.
- Click the Inbox icon from the main menu.
- Open the message from the client.
- Click Create an offer.
- Select a Gig. You can also click Change Gig to select a different one.
- Describe your offer and include the payment method, price, and delivery time.
- In the Define the scope area, add extra services and revisions.
- In Offer settings, set an expiry date or choose to skip the Gig Requirements.
- Optional: Click Save as template to reuse the offer later.
- Click Send offer.

Managing offers

  • You can click Withdraw Offer at any time before the client accepts it or before it expires.
  • Clients who do not see the service they need on your Gig page can click Request a Quote to ask for a custom offer.
  • When a client receives an offer, they can click Accept, Decline, or Ask for Changes.

You can find helpful tips in our Perfect proposal article.

FAQs

  • Custom offers must be between $5 USD and $20,000 USD.
  • The delivery time frame for a custom offer ranges from 1 to 90 days.
  • You can include up to five steps in a milestone custom offer, and you get paid as you complete each task.
  • Yes, you can set the number of revisions between zero and 20, or choose Unlimited.
  • Subscriptions are for repeat business and can recur daily, weekly, or monthly for up to six months.
  • Clients can still pay for pending custom offers while you are away. Ensure you have no pending offers before setting your account status to unavailable.

A freelancer’s guide to the Fiverr order process

Understanding your order’s status helps you track a project’s progress from the moment it’s placed until it’s officially completed. By checking the status through the order page, you can ensure your work is delivered on time, the client’s requirements are met, and your earnings are on their way.

Order process overview

After a client places an order with you, they need to submit the order requirements. Once they submit it, the order process starts, and you’re expected to deliver the work within the specified timeframe. Once you deliver, the client reviews the delivery and completes the order. If the client has feedback and requires changes, they can reject the delivery and request revisions. You’ll need to re-deliver the revised work.

Your revenue becomes available 14 days after the order is completed. For Seller Plus, TRS, and Pro Talent freelancers, the clearance period is 7 days.

Receiving an order

Once your Gig is approved, you become eligible to receive orders. You’ll get a notification each time a client places a new order.

Freelancers cannot initiate contact with new clients. Clients must reach out first, either by placing an order directly or by sending you a message. After a client places an order, all communication takes place through the Inbox.

Clients can also contact you before placing an order. In these cases, especially for customized or unique requests, you can send a Custom Offer that the client can review and purchase. Another way to receive new orders is by responding to project briefs, where clients share their needs, and you can submit personalized offers.

Before the order starts

  • The client needs to submit their order requirements before the order can officially begin. On the order page, you’ll find an option to send a reminder prompting the client to respond. Until requirements are submitted, the order’s status remains Incomplete and the order page displays Requirements Needed. If you already have enough information to get started, you can select Skip requirements to move the order status to In Progress.
  • If the client doesn’t submit the requirements within 14 days of the order creation date and you don’t skip them, the order will be automatically canceled.
  • Tip: Carefully review the client’s requirements to understand their vision. If something is missing or unclear, follow up with targeted questions. Aligning early helps you stay on track and produce a delivery that meets the client’s expectations.
  • Once the client submits the requirements, the order moves to In Progress status, and you’re expected to deliver within the specified timeframe. A countdown timer on the order page shows the time remaining until the delivery date.
  • Requesting a delivery extension
  • If you need additional time to complete an order, whether due to changes in scope, unclear requirements, or unexpected delays, you can request a delivery time extension. This option provides added flexibility and helps ensure you deliver high-quality work.
  • How to request an extension
    • Go to the order page and click Extend delivery date, located under the Deliver Now button.
    • Choose the new delivery date, add a brief explanation for the client, and click Send Request.
  • What happens next
    • The client receives your request and has 48 hours to respond.
    • If the client doesn’t respond within 48 hours, the request is automatically accepted.
    • You’ll receive a notification once the client approves or declines the request.
    • You may request an extension more than once, but frequent changes can impact the client’s experience. Use this option thoughtfully.
    • If the client declines, the original delivery time remains unchanged.
  • Note: Extensions add time to the original delivery date, not the current date. For example, if the original deadline was the 1st and you request 3 extra days on the 4th, the new deadline becomes the 4th (3 days added to the 1st). You can request up to 60 days per request.

Order Timeline

Order Timeline lets you map out your work as a step-by-step plan directly on the order page and share it with your client. Your client can follow your progress and know exactly where the order stands throughout the process.

Eligibility

Order Timeline is available for:

  • Single-payment orders placed from Gigs and custom offers
  • Orders with a value over $200
  • Orders with a delivery duration of over 7 days

Milestones, subscription, and Hourly orders are not eligible.

Setting up your Order Timeline
  • Once the client submits their requirements (or you skip them), a Create timeline button appears on the order page.
  • When you click it, the timeline is automatically pre-populated by AI based on your conversation with the client, your Gig, and the services you offer.
  • You can edit, remove, or add your own steps before finalizing.
  • If you’re not ready right away, select Maybe later.
  • You have up to 3 days from the order creation date to set up the timeline. After 3 days, the option is no longer available.

Note: Steps can only be added or updated before your first delivery. Once you’ve delivered, the timeline can’t be changed.

Step types

You can choose from preset steps or create your own. You can add up to 24 steps in total.

Step

Description

Order confirmed

Marks the start of the order. Cannot be modified or edited.

Draft

Automatically marked as done when you share a draft via the Share Draft feature.

Video call

Automatically completed if a Zoom meeting held through the Inbox lasted over 4 minutes. If the meeting was held elsewhere, mark it as done manually.

Progress update

A message update for the client on the order. Must be marked as done manually.

Custom

You define the step title, description, and target date. Can only be marked as done manually.

Expected delivery

Reflects your expected delivery date. Updates automatically if you extend your delivery time. Cannot be modified or edited.

Delays

If a step is delayed, it must be marked as done manually. Delayed steps remain visible on the order page even after the order is completed, until you mark them as done. Your client can click Ask for an update next to a delayed step to request a progress update from you.

Note: Order Timeline does not affect your Success Score or any other account statistics.

Mobile

Order Timeline is view-only on the Fiverr mobile app for both freelancers and clients. You cannot create or edit steps from mobile.

Sharing a delivery draft

The Share Draft feature lets you share work in progress with your client before your final delivery. This gives your client an early look at your work, keeps them informed, and helps you both stay aligned well before the final submission.

Sharing a draft can also be done through the Order Timeline or separately if the order isn’t eligible for that feature.

Eligibility

You can share a draft for any order amount for the following order types:

  • Single payment orders
  • Milestone orders
  • Subscription orders

Note: Hourly orders are not eligible for the Share Draft feature.

How to share a draft

There are three ways to access the Share Draft option:

  • From the order page
  • From the regular Inbox
  • From the Inbox drawer on the order page

To share a draft:

  • Click Share Draft.
  • In the pop-up window, add a message and upload the files you want to share. Adding a link is optional.
  • If you have multiple active orders with the same client, select which order the draft is for.
  • You’ll receive a confirmation message once the draft is sent.

What to know about drafts

  • Your client receives a notification and email when you share a draft.
  • The client can reply to the draft from the order page or Inbox.
  • A message is clearly displayed to the client indicating this is a draft, not the final delivery.
  • Drafts do not change the order status in any way and have no expiry timeframe.
  • Drafts are not considered revisions.
  • Files and images shared as a draft are protected with a Fiverr watermark to prevent unauthorized use.
  • Drafts are scanned for viruses using the same process as delivery files.
  • File size limits are the same as for delivery files.
  • Drafts do not affect your Success Score or any other account statistics.
  • Drafts cannot be shared on the mobile app.

Submitting your delivery

Before submitting your delivery, make sure everything is complete:

  • Review your work to ensure it meets the agreed-upon scope and quality.
  • All requirements provided by the client have been addressed.
  • If anything is unclear or missing, contact the client for clarification before delivering.
  • Double-check that your files are correctly named, formatted, and easy to open.
  • All relevant files, documents, or screenshots showing the completed work are included.
  • Use the delivery message to summarize what you’ve included and any important notes for the client.
How to deliver
  • Go to My Business > Orders (or open the order directly from your dashboard) and select the order.
  • Click the Deliver Now button.
  • Attach your delivery files in the pop-up window by clicking Upload Work.
    • You can select a delivery file to use as a sample in your Live Portfolio.
    • A single file is limited to 1 GB. If you don’t deliver a file, you’ll be prompted to confirm that no file is attached.
    • If your file size is too large, you may use alternative methods (e.g., a Dropbox link).
  • Describe your delivery in the Describe your delivery in detail section.
  • Click Deliver Work.

Tip: You can save your progress by clicking Save draft. When you’re ready to submit, reopen the draft and send it.

Note: The Deliver Now button should only be used to submit completed work or proof that work has been finished. Misusing the delivery button, such as sending empty, partial, or placeholder deliveries, may result in violations of our Terms of Service.

After your delivery is submitted

Once you submit your work, the order status updates to Delivered, and your delivery becomes available for the client’s review.

The client has three days to accept the delivery, request revisions, or request an extension to the review period. If the client doesn’t take action, the system automatically marks the order as Complete after three days. For Gigs that require shipping, the auto-completion period is 14 days.

If the client needs more time, they can extend the review period by up to 5 days. The order remains in Delivered status, and no re-delivery is required, as this isn’t a revision request. The client can extend the review period again if needed.

Managing revision requests

If the client requests revisions, the order status updates to In Revision, indicating that additional work or corrections are required. You’ll need to re-deliver the updated work based on the client’s feedback.

  • The number of revisions a client can request depends on what’s included in your Gig package or agreed-upon order scope.
  • While the order is In Revision, you can adjust the order (such as adding Gig Extras) or request a new delivery date.
  • After completing the required edits, resubmit the updated files using the Deliver Now button.
  • The order changes from In Revision to Delivered once you send the re-delivery.

Tip: Don’t panic: revision requests are a common part of freelance work. Carefully review the client’s notes, stay professional, and ask for clarification if the request is unclear. Communicate promptly if any revision falls outside the original scope, and provide a brief summary of what was updated in your re-delivery message.

Managing late or disputed orders

The Fiverr Resolution Center is designed to help you address and resolve disputes independently. If an order runs into issues or a dispute, it’s reflected in the order status:

  • The delivery time has passed. The client may cancel the order if you don’t respond. A Late status affects your on-time delivery metric. If you expect delays, communicate with the client as early as possible and request a delivery extension.
  • The order has been in Late status for 24 hours. At this stage, the client can cancel the order independently.
  • You have 30 days to submit a delivery from the day your client placed an order if it’s very late; otherwise, the order will be automatically canceled.
  • On the 15th day of this timeframe, you will receive an email with the number of days left.
  • The Resolution Center has been used to request a mutual cancellation, an extension of the delivery date, or an update.

Learn more with Using the Resolution Center.

Tip: Staying proactive helps you avoid these statuses. Communicate clearly, manage expectations early, and adjust timelines when necessary.

Order extras

You can offer additional work to your client through order extras during an active order.

How to add extras

  • From the Activity tab, select Offer more extras below the order page text box.
  • Choose to send existing extras or create a custom extra.
  • For custom extras: describe the extra, set a price, and include any additional days needed. Note that you must select an amount and time (even if 0 days), and extras cannot be priced at $0.

You can also send order extras from the mobile app. Clients can add order extras at the start of the order from the Activity tab, or during the order from the Details tab.

Completed orders

An order is marked as Complete once you deliver the work and the client accepts it. If the client takes no action within three days of delivery, the system automatically completes the order.

  • After completion, you’ll see a confirmation message showing the order is complete and displaying your earned revenue.
  • Once an order is completed, its status cannot be changed or canceled through the Resolution Center.
  • Revenue clearance: Your earnings become available 14 days after the order is completed. For Seller Plus, TRS, and Pro Talent freelancers, the clearance period is 7 days.
  • If the client has already left a review, you’ll be able to rate your experience with them as well.

Viewing & managing your orders

You can view and manage your orders on both web and mobile: My Business > Orders on the web, and Manage Orders on mobile.

  • ​
    • Priority: Orders that require your attention.
    • Active: Active orders where you work on the delivery.
    • Late: Orders placed late or very late that you didn’t deliver on time.
    • Delivered: Delivered orders waiting for the client to accept the delivery, or ask for a revision.
    • Completed: Orders that have been delivered by you and accepted by the client.
    • Cancelled: All canceled orders, either by Customer Support or mutually canceled orders.
    • Starred: Important orders marked by you.
  • ​
    • Updates: Orders with new messages or notifications.
    • Waiting for details: Orders where the client needs to submit the requirements to you before the order can start.
    • Active: All orders in all active statuses.
    • New: New orders that just started after the client submitted the requirements.
    • Late deliveries: Orders placed late or very late that you didn’t deliver on time.
    • Revision requested: Orders where the client declined delivery and requested revisions.
    • Completed: Orders that have been delivered by you and accepted by the client.
    • Waiting for rating: Orders where the client needs to review the delivery.
    • Cancelled: All canceled orders, either by Customer Support or mutually canceled orders.
Using external tools to manage your orders

You can use third-party tools to help organize your projects, but you are responsible for making sure they follow our Terms of Service. Section 8.8 prohibits using automated software or processes, such as bots, crawlers, or scrapers, to collect or extract data from Fiverr, and also prohibits doing so manually. Tools that automatically pull order, chat, or file data from Fiverr may violate this and can lead to account restrictions.

Fiverr can’t review or approve specific tools. If you store buyer information in an external system, you remain bound by the confidentiality obligations in section 8.10. Keep all communication and payments on Fiverr.

Best practices

  • Review requirements carefully before starting work and ask targeted follow-up questions if anything is unclear.
  • Communicate proactively with your client throughout the order, especially if you anticipate delays.
  • Use the Share Draft feature to share work in progress and get early feedback before your final delivery.
  • Request a delivery extension as early as possible rather than letting the order go late.
  • Always deliver completed work. Partial or placeholder deliveries violate Fiverr’s Terms of Service.
  • Stay professional during revision requests and provide clear summaries of what was updated in each re-delivery.
Best practices by category
- Upload a separate .jpg image file of the logo and select it for the Live Portfolio when delivering.
- Fiverr can add a watermark to delivered image files (jpg, png, etc.), which will be removed when the client accepts the final delivery.
- Note: The watermark is only added to files in the delivery message. It is not added to files sent through the inbox or order messages.
  • Follow these best practices for Digital Marketing Gigs:
    • Use Custom Offers and Milestones as a workaround for retainer/subscription-based work.
    • Provide a final report document in your delivery for Gigs that are more service-related than deliverable-related.
  • Note: Orders should be marked as delivered once the full service has been provided. Evidence of the work done should be sent as proof of delivery.
  • Use PDFs as an attachment to deliveries to show delivery samples in the Live Portfolio.
  • Use Dropbox or other file-sharing sites to deliver files that exceed the Fiverr upload limit.
    • We suggest providing a few screenshots or a screencast (video) of your final work to ensure you receive a client’s final approval before fully delivering your website design and development work (ex: source files and code).
    • Have a website design or programming order that has a few stages and milestones before final delivery? We suggest creating a custom offer that includes milestones. For example: consider creating three milestones to reflect each phase of the project. (First: Working on the mockup for approval; Second: Delivering the project based on the design; Third: Revising the order, if required + extra services, like SSL, hosting set-up, etc.)

FAQs

  • Your order automatically completes after 3 days (standard and hourly orders) or 8 days (milestone orders) if the client doesn’t request revisions or accept the delivery.
  • Yes. While your order is active (in progress, rejected, late, or very late), you can deliver as many times as needed.
  • A draft is a work-in-progress share that doesn’t count as a delivery, doesn’t change your order status, and doesn’t trigger autocomplete. A delivery is your formal submission that starts the 3-day review clock.
  • No. Steps can only be added or updated before your first delivery. Once you’ve delivered, the timeline is locked and can’t be changed.
  • No. Drafts have no impact on your Success Score or any other account statistics.
  • No. Only you can request a delivery extension. Your client can accept or decline the request.
  • Your client can extend the review period on their own without your approval. They can extend up to 5 days at a time and can do so an unlimited number of times.
  • Revenue becomes available 14 days after order completion. For Seller Plus, TRS, and Pro Talent freelancers, the clearance period is 7 days.

Hourly payment protection policy

Fiverr’s Hourly Payment Protection is a safeguard designed to ensure you get paid for your Hourly contracts, even in the event of a client’s payment failure. This policy supports freelancers who maintain transparency, clearly log their hours, and comply with all contract and policy requirements, allowing you to focus on your work with confidence.

All Fiverr Terms of Service and Fiverr Pro Terms of Service apply to Fiverr’s Hourly Payment Protection.

Overview

Hourly Payment Protection ensures that you are compensated for your logged time on Hourly orders if a client’s payment fails.

  • What it does: Compensates freelancers for work completed on Hourly orders when a client’s payment fails. Appropriate compensation is determined individually.
  • Why it’s useful: Provides a safeguard for freelancers, ensuring you get paid for your work and supporting those who log their hours clearly and stay within contract limits.
  • Who it’s for: Freelancers working on Hourly orders with a client.

Protection eligibility

To be eligible for Hourly Payment Protection and receive compensation in the event of a payment failure, you must meet all account and contract requirements and ensure your hours are clearly documented.

Allow seven days for the client to update their payment method. If the issue remains unresolved after that period, please contact Customer Support for further assistance.

  • To qualify for payment protection, your logged hours must:
    • Include a clear & specific task description.
    • Reflect only time you have actually worked.
    • Include supporting files like deliverables or screenshots, when applicable.
    • Be submitted before the weekly payment is due.
  • Important: Vague entries such as “test,” “work,” or empty fields may disqualify your hours. Additionally, logs that suggest you weren’t actively working are not covered.
  • To be eligible for Hourly payment protection, you must:
    • Have worked on an Hourly order with a client.
    • Stay within your weekly hour limit.
    • Use your account in compliance with Fiverr’s Terms of Service and Community Standards.
  • If your client fails to pay, follow these steps to activate your Hourly payment protection:
    • Stop all work on the order in question. The order will be automatically suspended, and you will no longer be able to log additional hours.
    • Wait as Fiverr contacts the client to resolve the payment issue.
    • If payment is not settled within 7 days, you will be entitled to receive compensation.
    • Reach out to Customer Support.
    • Request compensation for your Hourly order and provide relevant details.
  • Fiverr will review your logged hours, and if all criteria are met, you will be compensated for that billing cycle.

What’s not covered?

Hourly Payment Protection does not apply to:

  • Hours that exceed your weekly contract limit or were logged after the payment failure.
  • Tips, milestones, extras, subscriptions, or fixed-price projects.
  • Task descriptions that are vague, empty, irrelevant, or fake.
  • Logs that suggest you weren’t actively working.
  • Any disputes that are not related to the payment (client rejects the weekly report).
  • Any misuse of this policy or breach of Fiverr’s Terms, which shall render an Hourly order ineligible for payment protection, as determined at Fiverr’s sole discretion.

Hourly work for freelancers

The hourly work option is an addition to your current fixed-price model, giving you more flexibility to accommodate any project and build long-term client relationships.

It allows eligible freelancers and agencies to work and get paid on an hourly basis. By offering hourly rates, you can expand your service offerings and attract clients with diverse project needs. This feature also provides flexibility for projects where the scope might change as they unfold.

Overview

Hourly work is ideal when the project scope is unclear or likely to evolve, when the client wants to secure your availability for a long-term project, or when the time estimation exceeds 8 hours. For projects less than one working day, a fixed-price service is recommended.

Before you begin

  • The hourly work option is available to freelancers at Level One and above.
  • The custom hourly offer must have a minimum time estimation of 8 hours.

How Hourly works

When working on an hourly order, you’ll manage your hours and project progress directly through the Fiverr order page.

  • Set your rate: You can set or change your hourly rate on your freelancer page.
  • Custom offers: Use hourly rates when creating a Custom Offer based on a client’s request.
  • Automatic payments: Track your hours and receive weekly automatic payments.

Setting up your Hourly rate

You can set your preferred hourly rate on the dedicated hourly rate setup page in your freelancer profile.

  • On your freelancer profile, locate the Set your hourly rate option in the left-hand sidebar.
  • Enter your desired hourly rate (e.g., 25.00) and click Save.
  • This rate is optional and will be visible on your profile and in the search results when the “hourly rate” filter is activated.
  • To change your hourly rate, click on Change under the Hourly rate section, enter your new rate, and click Save. You can also delete your current hourly rate here.

How to create a custom Hourly offer

When sending a Custom Offer to a client through your inbox, you can choose the offer type.

  • Select the Gig for which you’d like to create an hourly custom offer.
  • Click Hourly to create a custom hourly offer.
  • Set up the offer, including the hourly rate.
    • Optional: Add a weekly hour limit.
  • Provide the client with an estimated total number of hours for the project (minimum of 8 hours).
    • Optional: Set a Custom Offer expiration.
  • Click on Send offer.

Important: It’s recommended to communicate the expected weekly hours to the client to increase transparency. The client can change the weekly limit once the order is placed. Providing a time estimation helps increase client trust.

How to report your working hours

You will be able to report the hours you worked manually on the order page.

Hours must be logged each week by Sunday, 23:59 UTC.

  • In the activity tab, click the Report hours button.
  • In the How many hours did you work section, select the total time you worked (including both hours and minutes).
  • Briefly describe what you accomplished during those reported hours.
  • Add a more detailed description of your work and attach any relevant files to provide additional context for the client.
  • Click the Submit hours button.

Provide as much detail as possible: Include a detailed description of the tasks performed, attach deliverables, supporting documents, and screenshots, as this will increase transparency with the client and help us protect your work if the client files a dispute.

Feedback

Clients will be able to leave a review during an in-progress hourly order when two conditions are met:

  • At least four weeks of work have been done.
  • The freelancer has reported at least 10 hours of work.

You will be able to respond to the feedback once the client has left it.

Payments and disputes

Once you submit your weekly report, your client is charged the following Monday.

  • The client has 7 days (until next Monday) to approve or dispute the report. Starting from the second week, they can enable automatic approval.
  • If your client doesn’t approve or dispute within 7 days, your report will be auto-approved, and your payment will follow within the next 7 days.
  • Once your client approves the report, your funds will be added to your balance within 14 days or 7 days, if you have a Seller Plus subscription or are a TRS or Pro freelancer.
  • If the client disputes the weekly report, you must accept or decline their request within 48 hours. You can offer a full or partial refund through the Resolution Center. If you don’t respond within 48 hours, the weekly report is automatically canceled. Learn more with partial refunds.
  • Hourly orders come with Fiverr-backed protection, ensuring you will be paid for every hour of work performed, as long as your reported hours meet our Hourly protection policy.
  • Learn more with the Hourly payment protection policy.

Suspended Orders

An order will be suspended if the client’s payment method is not successfully processed. Once the client updates the payment method, the order will resume, and you can continue working.

While they update their payment method, stop the work you are doing.

If the client doesn’t update their payment method within 7 days, please contact our Customer Support.

Ending an Hourly order

You or the client can end an order by clicking the sidebar and selecting ‘End order’. Once the order is ended, you’ll have 24 hours to log any remaining hours, which will then require the client’s approval the following Monday.

FAQs

  • Should a client’s payment fail, the order will be suspended, and you will be paid for the time you log in your weekly report as long as your reported hours meet our Hourly protection policy.
  • Once the client ends the order, you will have 24 hours to log in any additional hours you have worked on. The client will be charged the following Monday.
  • Hourly rates follow a weekly billing cycle, which ends every Sunday:
    • Once your client approves your weekly report: Your funds will be available within 7 days.
    • If your client doesn’t approve or dispute within 7 days: Your report will be automatically approved, and your payment will follow within another 7 days.
    • Overall timing: You’ll receive your funds 7–14 days after the billing cycle ends, depending on how quickly your client takes action.
  • Note: If the client doesn’t manually approve the first week’s report, you’ll still be compensated. However, the hourly order will be paused for 3 months, unless the client returns and reactivates it. If the client doesn’t take any action after auto-approval, the order will be paused for 3 months and then auto-complete.
  • To enhance transparency with clients, it’s important to: include a detailed description of the tasks performed, attach deliverables, supporting documents, and screenshots, and utilize an external tracking system for added clarity. This allows you to add the number of hours worked down to the minute. Please keep in mind that this is a beta version, and a built-in tracking system may be available in the future.
  • The hourly pricing model is an optional addition to your current fixed rate model. If it isn’t relevant to your expertise or services, you don’t have to adopt it.
  • Not to worry, it’s just another way to work and expand your services.
  • For help determining your rates, refer to this article. And remember that once you set it up, you can always change the rate in the custom hourly offers as needed.
  • For now, you can only work by the filter, and the client can set a weekly limit.
  • You can only set up one hourly rate for all of your services, and this rate will be displayed on your profile. However, should a client inquire about your services, you have the flexibility to send a custom hourly offer based on their unique requirements.
  • You can change your hourly rate directly from your profile. You can also change the rates outlined in custom hourly offers.
  • Hourly orders come with Fiverr-backed protection, ensuring freelancers will be paid for every hour of work performed. Clients are billed automatically once a week, and can request refunds on a week-by-week basis—not for the entire order. Learn more with Hourly payment protection policy.
  • Yes. Clients can see and choose hourly rates when they:
    • Filter marketplace search results to show only freelancers with hourly rates.
    • Create a brief with the option to select hourly rates.
    • Visit your Gig or profile page.

How order disputes work for freelancers

Managing order disputes is an important part of using Fiverr. You can request to cancel an active order through the Resolution Center when issues arise. This article explains the types of order disputes, how to cancel an order, and how order disputes can affect your performance. Our goal is to reach the fairest outcome for you and your client.

Before you begin

  • You can access the Resolution Center from the right side of the order page.
  • The Resolution Center is used for orders that have not yet been completed. If you need to cancel a completed order, contact Customer Support.

Ways to avoid order disputes

An order dispute is a cancellation request you send through the Resolution Center when you want to cancel an order.

While order disputes are sometimes unavoidable, taking a proactive approach before and during an order can help prevent them and improve your Order Completion Rate.

  • Follow these tips before an order begins:
    • Be clear about the pricing and scope of your Gig. Only offer services you are qualified to deliver.
    • Accurately display your latest and original work on your Gig page.
    • Communicate all necessary details in your Gig description, requirements, and extras in advance.
    • If a client is unresponsive from the start, initiate a mutual cancellation through the Resolution Center.
  • Follow these tips during an active order:
    • Communicate with your client throughout the order. If you are unsure about the project, contact your client for clarification.
    • Set realistic delivery times. If you often feel the need to cancel because you are too busy, give yourself more time to deliver or ask to extend the delivery date.
    • If you need to change the delivery date or add extra services, use the order page to modify the order instead of canceling. You can extend the delivery date or offer more extras directly from the order page.
    • If you require more time to deliver, communicate this clearly with your client through the order chat, and then use the Resolution Center if necessary.
    • Use Share Draft to share work in progress before your final delivery. The client can give feedback early, and we use drafts to understand how the order progressed if a dispute happens.
    • If you use the Order Timeline, keep the steps and dates current, and tell the client about any delay. We review the timeline to understand how an order progressed, but a delayed timeline step does not make an order late.
  • Learn more about sharing drafts and Order Timeline with A freelancer’s guide to the Fiverr order process.
  • If you know you will not be able to work on your Gig, pause it. Reactivate it when you are available so clients know you can complete it.
  • Use the Availability feature to manage your schedule:
    • Set the time and date you will be away.
    • Add a short note explaining your availability.
    • Activate the feature. It deactivates automatically at the end of your leave period.
  • Start with your simplest orders first. For larger projects, start earlier than you normally would.
  • If you find yourself pausing your Gig often, consider limiting your order intake to avoid getting overbooked.
  • Learn more with Setting availability for freelancers.

Delivering an empty message or sending incomplete work to avoid a late delivery is a violation of Fiverr’s Terms of Service and may result in your account being reviewed.

Types of order disputes

There are several types of order cancellations on Fiverr, depending on who initiates the request and when.

  • Clients can request to cancel an active order at any time through the Resolution Center. Once the client submits the request, you have 48 hours to accept or decline. If you do not respond, we cancel the order automatically.
  • Sometimes canceling an order is the best way to resolve an ongoing order issue. If you request to cancel, the client has 48 hours to respond. If the client does not respond within 48 hours, we cancel the order automatically.
  • In some situations, clients can cancel without your approval:
    • Before submitting project requirements: If a client placed an order and has not yet submitted their project requirements, they can cancel immediately through the Resolution Center.
    • Very late delivery: If you have not delivered and you did not both agree to extend the delivery date, the client can cancel without approval after 24 hours past the expected delivery date.
  • Learn more about meeting your deadlines with Avoiding late deliveries.
  • Note: If something outside your control stops you from completing an order, contact Customer Support. Examples include a natural disaster, a government-imposed outage or restriction, a global event that disrupts your work, or a serious illness or emergency. We review each case.

We can cancel an active order when we confirm a violation of our Terms of Service, such as fraud, a fake identity, stolen or non-original work, harassment or discrimination, a false or empty delivery, or a prohibited service.

How to cancel an order

You can request a cancellation through the Resolution Center on the order page. To access the Resolution Center:

  • Go to your Orders page and select the order you want to resolve, then click View.
  • Click Resolution Center, located on the right side of the page.
  • Select Cancel Order and fill in the reason.
  • Click Send Request.

Learn more with Cancel an order with the Resolution Center.

Canceling an order with an open request

If you want to cancel an order with an open Resolution Center request, you need to withdraw the request first on the Orders page. After withdrawing the request, you can submit a cancellation request.

You cannot open a new cancellation dispute while any of the following actions are in progress:

  • Get an order update
  • Cancel order
  • Extend delivery date

If the order is in completed status, you cannot use the Resolution Center to cancel it. If you cannot resolve the issue together, contact Customer Support.

Cancellations & performance

When we evaluate your performance, we take all cancellations into account. Some cancellations are unavoidable and have a lower impact on performance scores.

Order Completion Rate

Order completion refers to successfully completing an order, where a client receives and approves the service they ordered. Your Order Completion Rate (OCR) is part of your overall Success Score, alongside other performance factors. Cancellations can impact your performance, but they are just one factor in your overall Success Score.

Learn more with the Success Score article.

OCR impact by scenario:

  • Orders canceled by the client before they submit their project requirements: no impact on your OCR.
  • Very late orders force-canceled by the client: your OCR is affected.
  • Orders in which you submit the cancellation request: your OCR is affected.

Keeping a steady Order Completion Rate helps you build strong client relationships and grow your business on Fiverr.

FAQs

  • Go to your Orders page, select the order, and click Resolution Center. Click Cancel order, enter a message, select a reason, and click Send Request. The client has 48 hours to accept or decline. If they do not respond, we cancel the order automatically.
  • No. You cannot force-cancel an order. The client must approve your cancellation request, or we cancel the order automatically after 48 hours.
