Can’t find your Gig?

Clients find services on Fiverr by searching with keywords that match what they need. When a client searches, eligible Gigs may appear in the search results. Gig visibility can vary based on factors such as performance, competition, and system processes. This article explains why your Gig may not appear in search and what steps you can take to improve its visibility.

How Gig search works

Fiverr search is designed to show clients the most relevant services based on their needs. Gig placement in search results is determined by an algorithm that considers multiple quality and business-related signals over time to deliver fair, useful, and competitive results.

These following factors help deliver optimized and personalized search results on Fiverr:

  • Search placement reflects how your Gig performs across several quality and business metrics compared to others in the marketplace, including:
    • Relevance: How closely your Gig’s title, description, and metadata match a client’s search query.
    • Historical performance: How attractive your Gig has been to clients with similar needs in the past.
    • Satisfaction: Client review scores and overall purchase satisfaction.
    • Responsiveness: How quickly and effectively you communicate with clients.
  • Fiverr aims to show services that are the best fit for each individual search, rather than a single fixed ranking. Search results may vary from client to client based on:
    • The specific keywords used in the search
    • The client’s needs, preferences, and past activity
  • Search results are continuously adjusted to improve relevance and marketplace health. This includes:
    • Results include a range of pricing options to help clients compare and choose from multiple price ranges
    • Updating rankings as new performance data is collected
    • Ensuring fair visibility for high-quality services over time

Why your Gig might not appear in search

You’ve put effort into creating your Gig, so it can be frustrating if you can’t find it in search results. Your Gig may be temporarily unavailable or harder to find for one of the following reasons:

  • Your Gig may be flagged by our Trust & Safety team if the content in your description, images, or video doesn’t fully follow Fiverr’s Terms of Service or Community Standards. While under review, your Gig may not appear in search.
  • If you’ve made edits or updates to your Gig, it may temporarily disappear from search while our system re-indexes the information. Give it a bit of time after making updates, and it should reappear.
  • In popular categories, many freelancers offer similar services. Even well-optimized Gigs can be harder to find due to high competition and get lost in the crowd. Consider if your Gig can be more niche or offer a unique angle to help it stand out.
  • Improve your Gigs by implementing some best practices.
  • Metrics like late deliveries, cancellations, or low response rates can affect how often your Gig appears in search.
  • Improve your performance with Best practices for freelancers.

If a Gig violates Fiverr policies, it may be removed from search or taken down entirely.

How to improve your Gig’s visibility

If your Gig is active but difficult to find, improving its quality and clarity can help it stand out.

You can try the following best practices:

  • Add a Gig video: In your Adding and managing your Gig video clearly explain your service and what clients can expect.
  • Update your visuals: For the best Gig images, use clear, high-quality images that reflect your unique service.
  • Refine your description: Accurately describe your unique services to become attractive to clients. Keep it easy to read and transparent.
  • Add FAQs: Address common client questions to set expectations early and clarify your offering.
  • Utilize Fiverr tools: Benefit from Fiverr programs such as Fiverr Ads or the Seller Plus Program, which includes Advanced Analytics tools like Top Keywords and Keyword Research, to help maximize your Gig’s visibility in search results.

Join Fiverr’s Community for more tips on optimization and become part of a supportive network that helps you succeed on the platform

How to share your services

You can share your Fiverr profile or specific Gigs to promote your services and reach clients outside Fiverr.

  • Share your profile: Go to Growth & Marketing > Scale Your Business, then copy your profile URL or select a social icon to share.
  • Share a specific Gig: Go to My Business > Gigs, click the drop-down menu next to your Gig, select Share, and choose your preferred platform.

Sharing your profile or Gigs is fully allowed, as long as your promotions follow Terms of Service and accurately represent the services you offer.

FAQs

  • A consistent personal brand can help. Use a clear profile image, a focused description, and well-defined services so clients immediately understand what you offer.
  • Review your delivery times, responsiveness, and order completion. Make sure your work is original, deadlines are met, and client messages are answered promptly.

Creating & editing your freelancer profile

Your profile is how you showcase your expertise and professional appearance to the community. By providing a complete and authentic profile, you enhance your visibility and build trust with potential clients, establishing a reliable and professional presence on our platform.

How to initiate the process?

  • If you intend to become a freelancer in your account set up, you will automatically be navigated to create your freelancer profile. Create an account to become a Fiverr freelancer.
  • If you are selling for the first time, and already have an account, click on your Profile picture > “Become a Seller”.
  • To switch your account to “Selling” mode, the first step is to complete the freelancer onboarding process. To complete the onboarding process access this link to complete the freelancer onboarding process.

Profile creation and editing are currently only supported on desktop platforms and web mobile devices. App (Android and iOS) do not support these functions.

How to create your freelancer profile?

To create and complete your freelancer profile, choose if you would like to upload your experience with an existing CV or Resume, or add your profile information manually.

Upload your experience

  • Upload a PDF of your resume, CV, or an export from LinkedIn profile.
  • Note: PDF files uploaded can be up to 10 megabytes.
  • Review each section and edit or fill in any missing information. For more information on each section of your freelancer profile, see the Add experience manually tab.
  • Click “Continue” to create your profile.

Add experience manually

  • Your display name will be visible to all clients. We recommend you use your first name and the first letter of your last name. Using your real name or a consistent professional identity helps buyers feel confident they are working with a genuine freelancer which supports a safer, more trustworthy marketplace. If you need to edit your display name, or want inspiration, find additional information in managing your display name.
  • Your profile picture is an essential part of your professional identity on Fiverr. It’s an opportunity to present yourself to potential clients, giving them a better sense of who you are and building trust and confidence before you even start working together.
  • When selecting your profile picture, keep these key guidelines in mind:
    • Personal presence and authenticity: Show yourself clearly. Choose a recent, authentic photo where you are the sole focus. Using images of other people, celebrities, or GIFs is not allowed. If you run an agency, you may use your company logo.
    • Use of AI tools: You may use AI tools to enhance the quality of your image, such as improving lighting or refining the background. However, the use of AI-generated avatars is strictly prohibited. Your photo must be a genuine representation of your actual appearance.
    • Professional quality: Ensure your image is high-resolution, clear, and well-lit. Use a simple, uncluttered background so the focus remains entirely on you.
  • Stand out with a short tagline that describes what you do. Avoid using any descriptive words (like “expert”, “best” or “Fiverr”) in your Title. Keep your title truthful and aligned with the services you offer. Realistic, accurate titles help clients find the right freelancer and support a fair and transparent marketplace experience.
  • Your location is set when you register your account and is determined according to the country from where you register. Your country is displayed on your profile for transparency, which helps users understand differences in language and time zones. Fiverr also uses this information to comply with local regulations, such as tax requirements.
  • Read more about managing your account settings.
  • If your account location is incorrect, you will need to contact Customer Support to request a change. You will be required to provide proof of residency which must include your name and current address.
  • We accept the following documents as proof of residency:
    • Utility bills
    • Telephone bills
    • Rental agreements
  • If you are an ID-verified freelancer, the name on your proof of residency must match the name on the ID you used for verification.
  • We do not accept the following documents as proof of residency:
    • Government-issued IDs (e.g., passports, national IDs, driver’s licenses)
    • Residency or student visa permits
    • Tax returns
  • Highlight your language skills to make your freelancer profile stand out and communicate with a wider audience! List all the languages you can work in and include your proficiency level for each.
  • The About section gives you the chance to introduce yourself to potential clients. Clients rely on the About section to better understand you as a professional! Titles should be accurate, authentic and aligned with Fiverr’s policies to help protect yourself and your clients.
  • Writing about you
    • Be honest and accurately represent yourself and your experiences.
    • Be clear and write in English without grammatical errors.
    • Be original!
    • Do not include contact information including payment information and personal phone numbers or emails, company names, or URLs.
    • Do not offer services that infringe on Fiverr TOS or 3rd parties TOS. Learn more about our community standards and prohibited services.
  • Note: Ensure you add a space after the last period of each sentence or this section will not save properly. For instance, “example. example”.
  • Add specific skills and areas of expertise to your profile to help ensure the right clients find you. List all your skills and include your experience level. Include the software, tools, and techniques you use, as well as areas of expertise you specialize in. Describing your skills and experience honestly helps set a client’s expectations, builds long-term trust, and prevents misunderstanding or disputes later on.
  • Add your job history and achievements to give clients insights into your expertise.
  • Note: If your company was rejected, we cannot manually review and approve it.
  • Showcase your skills and qualifications by adding any degrees you’ve earned and the institutions where you studied.
  • Showcase your mastery with certifications earned in your field.

Finishing your profile

Once you’re done, click Continue to create your freelancer profile. You will be asked if you work as an individual or team and you have the option to add personal website links, which will not be shared with other users.

You will then be navigated to your freelancer dashboard. To make your profile visible to clients, just complete the New freelancer onboarding tasks on your dashboard. This helps you get set up for success and ready to start working.

If you leave the page during the profile creation process, your progress will be saved.

Tip: Stand out to potential clients and add a Fiverr intro video.

Editing your profile

To edit your existing freelancer profile, go to your dashboard and click “View profile.” Locate the current field you wish to edit then click the pencil to edit the information. Make sure you click save to keep the changes made.

Connect your Fiverr profile to LinkedIn

Pro and Top Rated freelancers can connect their Fiverr accounts to LinkedIn. Once connected, Fiverr will appear in LinkedIn’s Connected Accounts section. Your LinkedIn profile will display a Fiverr credibility signal and capability statement that reflects the services you provide on Fiverr backed by your proven expertise, making your real-world expertise visible to prospective clients who are searching for talent.

  • You can connect your accounts from any of these entry points on your Fiverr freelancer account:
    • Dashboard message: A prompt in your freelancer dashboard invites you to connect your LinkedIn profile.
    • Profile Strength on the Dashboard: A “Connect your LinkedIn” action appears as a recommended step in your Profile Strength checklist until the connection is made. It flips to complete once you authorize.
    • Seller profile self-view: The LinkedIn card on your profile page lets you manage the connection, with the option to disconnect, at any time.
  • Once you click any of these entry points, follow these steps:
    • Click Connect to LinkedIn.
    • You will be redirected to LinkedIn. Log in if prompted.
    • Click Allow to authorize Fiverr to access your LinkedIn profile.
    • You will be returned to Fiverr and see a connection confirmation message.
  • To connect your Fiverr account from your LinkedIn profile, follow these steps:
    • From your LinkedIn profile, click Add section.
    • Click Add connected account.
    • Choose Fiverr from the list.

FAQs

  • Ensure you complete all onboarding tasks located on your freelancer dashboard to become visible to clients.
  • Your display name should be written in English without special characters other than period or apostrophe and reflect your real name or the name of your business. Keep it true to who you are and avoid using someone else’s name or choosing a name that doesn’t relate to your identity. There’s no need to include your services, profession, or any descriptive words (like “expert” or “best”) in your display name. You can highlight those details in your Title instead. Also, please don’t reference Fiverr levels in your display name.
  • Profile pictures must be unique and original photographs that represent you or the service you offer! Profile pictures should not be of another person, of a celebrity, be a GIF, or it should not misrepresent the service that you provide.
  • Check first that you are uploading your CV or Resume in PDF format. Next, check that your file size does not exceed 10 megabytes.
  • You can also download a PDF of your LinkedIn profile to upload as your freelancer profile on Fiverr.
  • You must complete your freelancer profile to be able to switch to your freelancer account. You can access this link to complete your profile. Follow the on screen instructions and fill out all mandatory fields.

  • To switch your account to “Selling” mode, the first step is to complete the freelancer onboarding process. To complete the onboarding process, you can follow these steps:

    • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete all mandatory fields.

  • For Pros, if your capability statement on the Fiverr connected accounts in LinkedIn does not accurately reflect your work, please contact our Customer Support team.
  • Yes. Go to the LinkedIn card on your seller profile self-view page and select the disconnect option. You can also remove the Fiverr connection from LinkedIn from the same card.

  • Fiverr capability statements are backed by a vetting process that evaluates freelancers based on proven expertise, professional experience, portfolio quality, communication skills, and ongoing performance. Fiverr’s in-house experts assess each freelancer’s specialization and ability to consistently deliver high-quality results, while client reviews, reliability, and satisfaction help maintain Fiverr standards over time. If your capability statement does not accurately reflect your services, please reach out to Support who can help remove it.

Creating a Gig

Your Gig is how you offer services on Fiverr. It’s your storefront, the place where clients learn what you do, what’s included, and how to place an order. This article walks you through each step of creating, configuring, and publishing your first Gig.

Overview

A Gig consists of a title, category, pricing packages, a description, requirements, and a media gallery. Once you publish, your Gig goes through an automatic review and if it meets Fiverr’s policies, becomes visible to clients in the marketplace.

Gig creation is only available on desktop.

Before you begin

Make sure you have the following in place before you create your first Gig:

  • Complete your freelancer profile. If you haven’t switched to selling yet, you’ll need to complete the freelancer onboarding process first.
  • Use a desktop browser. Gigs can only be created and edited from a desktop device.
  • Review Fiverr’s Gig policies and Prohibited Services guidelines before you get started. Gigs that don’t comply won’t be approved.
  • Make sure the service you plan to offer complies with Fiverr’s Community Standards and doesn’t violate the Terms of Service.
  • Check your Gig allowance. The number of Gigs you can have active at once depends on your freelancer level:
    • New freelancers: up to 4 Gigs
    • Level 1 and Level 2: up to 10 Gigs
    • Top Rated: up to 30 Gigs

If you’ve reached your limit, you’ll need to delete an existing Gig before you can create a new one.

Steps to create your Gig

To get started, go to My Business > Gigs > Create a New Gig, or click your profile picture and select Create a New Gig.

Step 1: Overview

This section sets the basic identity of your Gig.

  • Write a clear, descriptive title that tells clients exactly what you offer. Fiverr pre-fills the start of the title with “I will…” complete it from there.
    • Keep it specific and client-focused.
    • Avoid special characters such as &, /, “, and +.
  • Editing your Gig title later doesn’t change its URL.
  • Select the category and subcategory that best match your service. Choose carefully, you can’t change the category after the Gig is published.
  • Some categories are vetted-only, meaning Fiverr’s team must evaluate and approve you before you can create Gigs in them.
  • Add up to five words or short phrases that describe your Gig. These help Fiverr categorize your service in the right context.
  • Add up to five tags to improve your Gig’s visibility in search. Use short, relevant keywords that reflect what your clients are likely to search for.
Step 2: Scope & pricing
  • You can offer up to three packages: Basic, Standard, and Premium to give clients options at different price points. Use the Offer packages toggle in the top right to switch between a single flat rate and a multi-package setup.
  • For each package, set:
    • A delivery time (in days)
    • A revision count
    • A price (in USD)
  • Fiverr requires you to offer at least one revision option per package. If your work involves significant customization or creative output, consider offering more.
  • Prices are set in US dollars, regardless of your local currency. The minimum starting price is $5, though some categories have a higher minimum.
  • You can offer optional add-ons that clients can purchase during checkout. One common option is Extra Fast Delivery, which lets you charge more for a faster turnaround; the accelerated delivery time must be shorter than your standard one.
Step 3: Description & FAQ
  • Write a description of your Gig (up to 1,200 characters). Be specific enough that clients know exactly what they’re getting and whether your Gig fits their needs.
  • If your Gig involves a longer or more complex project, you can break it into milestones. This gives clients visibility into the project stages and helps you manage delivery expectations.
  • Add up to 10 frequently asked questions to reduce back-and-forth before orders are placed. Good topics to cover include delivery time, revision limits, what’s included in each package, and any service-specific details.
Step 4: Requirements

Use this section to ask clients for any information you need before you can start their order. You can mark individual questions as required to prevent orders from starting without the necessary details.

Step 5: Gallery
  • You must upload at least one image to publish your Gig. You can add up to three images.
    • Use images you own; no copyrighted material or images sourced from the internet.
    • Samples of your work make strong Gig images.
    • Recommended size: 1280 x 769 px at 72 DPI.
    • Minimum size: 712 x 430 px at 72 DPI.
  • Videos are required for Gigs in the Video & Animation category and optional for all others. The video thumbnail takes priority and displays before your Gig images.
    • Length: 20–60 seconds.
    • File size: under 50 MB.
    • Do not include copyrighted audio, visuals, or watermarks you don’t own.
  • You can upload up to two PDFs to showcase document-based work samples. Only the first three pages of each PDF are displayed. This field is optional.
  • PDFs in your Gig gallery are for preview only; clients cannot download them.
Step 6: Publish
  • Before you publish, indicate whether you’re a US person. US-based freelancers are also required to submit a W-9 form. EU freelancers may need to complete a DAC7 form where applicable. All freelancers must complete personal and business information verification for compliance purposes.
  • If you haven’t already, complete phone verification before publishing.
  • Once all required steps are complete, click Publish Gig. Your Gig will go through an automatic review. If it meets Fiverr’s policies, it will be approved and become visible in the marketplace.
  • If your Gig includes a video, the Gig itself may be approved automatically, but the video stays pending until it’s reviewed separately.

Best practices

  • Keep your Gig consistent over time. If you fundamentally change the service you’re offering, for example, switching from logo design to voiceover work, Fiverr may remove the Gig from search results. The reviews, ratings, and portfolio on your Gig are tied to the original service. If you want to offer a new type of service, create a new Gig instead.
  • Use all five search tags. Relevant, specific tags significantly improve your Gig’s discoverability.
  • Add FAQs from the start. Pre-answering common questions reduces messages before orders and builds client confidence.
  • Upload high-quality images. Your Gig image is the first thing clients see; make it representative of your actual work.
  • Set realistic delivery times. Under-promising and over-delivering is better for your reviews than the reverse.
  • Batch your edits. If you need to update multiple things, do them together. Frequent small changes can cause temporary dips in visibility while the system re-indexes your Gig.

Gig requirements

Gig requirements let you collect everything you need from a client before you start an order. The more detailed and organized your requirements are, the smoother your work process will be and the better the results for your client.

Best practices for working with clients
  • Set expectations early. Ask for all details upfront so both you and your client know what to expect from the order.
  • Avoid misunderstandings. Review submitted requirements and follow up with any questions before you begin.
  • Save time. Collect all information at once instead of going back and forth during the order.
  • Review the client’s brief thoroughly before responding.
  • Thank the client for their order and ask any follow-up questions.
  • Explain your first step, for example, a storyboard, mockup, or initial sketch, and send it for their review before continuing.
  • Send progress updates every two to three days via the order chat.
Requirements by category

The sections below include ready-to-use requirement briefs for specific categories. Adjust them to fit your service and send them to your client when they place an order.

Animated explainers
  • Share the following details with your freelancer:
    • Describe the product or features the video should focus on.
    • Describe the main concept or idea.
    • Share your business name, contact information, and social media links.
    • Describe your target audience.
    • Provide references of videos you like.
    • Share your preferred timeline.
  • Be ready to answer the following questions:
    • Do you have a script, or do you need us to write one?
    • What platform will you use to share the video?
    • What is your preferred format and duration?
    • What would you like on the last screen? (for example, logo, contact details, or a call to action)
    • Do you need a voice-over? If yes, share your preferred gender, age, language, accent, and tone.
Development projects
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • Business name, contact information, and social media links.
    • Who is your target audience?
    • What is the goal of your website?
    • Do you want to be able to edit the website yourself?
    • Design references: logo, color scheme, typography, and any other inspiration.
    • Existing content such as copy, images, or videos.
    • Domain name and hosting credentials, if you already have them.
    • Any additional requirements.
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • Business name, contact information, and social media links.
    • Who is your target audience?
    • What is the goal of your store?
    • Do you have a store account? If yes, provide credentials. If not, which platform would you like to use?
    • Design references: logo and color scheme.
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • App name, brief description, required features, and business contact information.
    • Apple or Google developer account details.
    • Who is your target audience?
    • What is the goal of your app?
    • Design references: app logo, color scheme, typography, and any screens or wireframes.
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • Game name, overview, required features, and a game design document or spec sheet.
    • Target platform.
    • Reference games that reflect the concept.
    • Who is your target audience?
    • Design references: logo, color scheme, typography, and any existing assets.
Social media marketing
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • Business name, website, and social media links and credentials.
    • What does the business do and what problem does it solve?
    • Services or products offered.
    • Unique selling point and main call to action.
    • Marketing goals and KPIs.
    • Target audience (location, age, gender, interests).
    • Main competitors.
    • Brand guidelines: color scheme, fonts, voice, and tone.
  • Prepare the following information for your freelancer:
    • Brand book and visual guidelines.
    • Media kit: logo, photos, and videos.
    • FAQs to handle follower interactions (for example, business hours, support contact, service details).
  • Be ready to answer the following questions:
    • Is this for business or personal use?
    • What is the purpose of the content: driving organic traffic or thought leadership?
    • Who is the target audience?
    • What is the topic and tone of voice?
    • Do you have brand voice guidelines or existing content to reference?
    • Do you need SEO-optimized keywords? If yes, how many?
    • Should I conduct additional research, or do you have research to include?
    • What type of engagement do you expect from the content?

Best practices for setting up Gig requirements

  • Match your requirements to what you promise in your Gig. For example, if you offer background removal from images, ask for the image along with instructions on what to keep and what to remove.
  • Clients see your requirements before they place an order, so write them as clearly and carefully as the rest of your Gig.
  • Keep your list of requirements short. Ask only for what you need to deliver quality work; too many questions can frustrate clients before the order even starts.
  • Give clients detailed instructions, and include an example when you ask for a specific type of information. For example: “Attach your photo and describe what you would like removed.”
  • Mark critical requirements as required, and use multiple-choice or free-text questions depending on the type of answer you need.
  • Add a multiple-choice requirement that introduces one Gig Extra. For example, a freelancer offering proofreading services could ask, “Would you like comments on common grammar mistakes for $5 USD more?” with options such as “Yes, send me a custom offer,” “No thanks,” and “Tell me more.”
  • Highlight one Gig Extra at a time, so you do not overwhelm clients right after they place an order.
  • Add an optional, free-text requirement asking clients how they found your Gig, for example, through a Fiverr search, a web search, or a repeat order.
  • Review the responses regularly to see which channels bring in the most orders, and focus your marketing efforts there.
  • If a client does not submit their requirements, the order does not start. Send a message reminding them to complete this step, or use the reminder option on your order page if one is available.

    • Disable VPNs, ad blockers, and browser extensions.
    • Switch to a different browser or device.
    • If your Gig was denied after you made content changes, this usually means the core service was altered from what was originally published. In that case, create a new Gig in the category that matches the updated service, and keep your existing Gig consistent with its original offering if you plan to keep it active.
    • If the issue continues, open a Support ticket and include a screenshot of the full error message and your Gig URL.

    • An account-level task changed status, for example, identity verification expired or a tax form became required.
    • A category or metadata mismatch that requires correction.
  • Review all Gig tabs for warnings, fix any flagged content, and make sure your account tasks show as approved. Replace or remove any problematic gallery assets; you need at least one compliant image, then republish. If it reverts again, contact Support and ask them to identify the specific blocking rule.

    • The Gig is in Draft or paused. Videos won’t be reviewed until the Gig is published and active. Publish or unpause your Gig to start the review.
    • The upload didn’t complete correctly. A network hiccup can leave a placeholder stuck on Processing. Re-upload the file and save.
    • The file doesn’t meet the required specs: 20–60 seconds, 16:9 aspect ratio, minimum 1280x720 resolution, MP4 format (H.264 + AAC), up to 5 GB.
    • The filename contains special characters, emojis, or spaces. Rename it using only letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.

    • Re-encode the file using HandBrake or similar: MP4, H.264, AAC 128 kbps, constant frame rate, 16:9 frame size with no black bars. Enable “Web Optimized” or “Fast Start” so the metadata sits at the start of the file.
    • Rename the file simply (for example: my_gig_video.mp4) and re-upload.
    • Upload from a desktop browser with extensions disabled, cache cleared, and no VPN active.
    • If the video is still stuck after 7 days on an active, published Gig, contact Support with screenshots and a screen recording of your upload steps.
  • Avoid uploading the same video multiple times in rapid succession. Upload once with the corrected file and wait 24–48 hours before following up.
  • No. PDFs added to your Gig gallery are for preview only. Clients can view them directly on your Gig page, but downloading is not available. To keep previews loading quickly, use compressed, well-organized PDFs and avoid very large file sizes.
  • Edits don’t reset your impression history, but they can affect current and future visibility:
    • Title, description, and pricing: Optimizing these generally won’t hurt long-term ranking, but the system may need time to re-index your Gig, which can cause a temporary dip in impressions.
    • Tags: Changing keywords affects which searches you appear in. If you target narrower or lower-volume terms, impressions can drop. Aim for accurate, client-aligned keywords.
    • Thumbnail and gallery media: Stronger visuals that match client intent tend to improve click-through rate. Weaker visuals can reduce it.
    • Video: Adding or replacing a video can improve engagement but may trigger a short re-indexing period.
    • Manual review: Some edits trigger a review, during which your Gig’s visibility may be limited for up to 48 hours.
  • Best practice: batch meaningful improvements together rather than making frequent small changes, and monitor your impressions and clicks for at least 7–14 days after any update.
  • Service types are a way to classify your Gig in subcategories that offer multiple kinds of services within a subcategory; they’re almost subcategories inside of subcategories. By tagging your Gig with the relevant service type, you can indicate what type of service you are offering in a specific Gig, and make sure that clients will easily find your Gig.
  • For example, within the WordPress subcategory, there are a variety of services to provide, so we identified the following service types:
    • Full website creation.
    • Customization.
    • Bug fixes.
    • Backup, Cloning & Migration.
    • Security.
    • Landing page.
    • WP installation & Set up.
    • Performance & SEO.
    • Help & Consultation.
  • You can select one service type per Gig.
  • First of all, be sure to activate Gig packages if available in your subcategory. You may see a prompt to add service types to your Gig when service types arrive in your subcategory. Or you can follow these steps:
    1. Go to Edit Gig.
  • 2. Select the right service type from the Pricing tab on the dropdown menu.
  • You will have the option to identify the correct service type when creating a Gig.
  • Tagging your Gig with the appropriate service type means defining it in the marketplace in a meaningful way for search results. The service type is essentially metadata that relates to terms that clients search for. When you use the right service type, clients who are looking for exactly what you provide will see your service in their search results. Picking a service type that fits your Gig will unlock the package attributes that allow you to better define what’s unique about your Gig.
  • Service types are not relevant to all subcategories because not every subcategory has multiple types of services available within it.

Creating and managing Gig packages

Gig packages are a pricing structure that lets you build service tiers by combining your basic Gig with revisions and extras. Packages give you the flexibility to position your services at any price point, help clients order exactly what they need in one click, and ensure everyone is aligned on scope before the order begins. For select categories, we apply standardized package requirements to keep offerings consistent and comparable across the platform.

Before you begin

  • To set up packages, you need an active Gig or you need to be in the process of creating one.
  • Access package settings from the Pricing section in the Gig create & edit flow.
  • If your Gig is in a standardized category, review the category requirements before making changes to ensure your packages meet the minimum standards.

Gig packages functionality

Packages let you offer up to three service tiers that clients can compare and choose from. Each tier can include a different scope of work, number of revisions, and extras. Clients can also add upgrades at checkout.

Packages include two types of add-ons:

  • Upgrades: predefined factors clients can add to a selected package at checkout
  • Extras: unique add-ons you can offer separately, but cannot include in a package

Our standard service fee applies to all packages, and packages do not affect your ratings.

Standardized Gig packages

For certain categories, we require standardized packages to improve catalog quality and help clients compare offerings across the platform. Standardized packages set a minimum service scope for each package in your Gig. If your Gig is in one of these categories, you must meet the minimum requirements to keep your Gig active and visible.

Category

Sub & Nested Category

Min Price

Programming & Tech

Mobile Apps → Full App Creation

$100

Video & Animation

3D Product Animation

$100

Data

Data Science → Full Project

$80

WordPress

Full Website Creation

$80

AI Services

AI Artists (e.g., Midjourney)

$15

Standardization types

We apply the following standardization elements to define what your packages must include:

  • Service type sits within the category tree, one level inside the subcategory. Choosing the right service type ensures your Gig reaches the right clients and uses the correct pricing and metadata for your service.
  • Some metadata at the Gig level is mandatory. Completing these fields helps search and browse filters show your Gig to the right clients.
  • Some elements involve a quantity (such as words, seconds, pages, or hours) that your package must include. There are two types:
  • Minimal scope: the quantity in your package must equal or exceed this value.
  • Fixed value: a specific quantity that all Gigs in the category must use for the same scope of work.
  • A pricing element that is an integral part of the service type. You cannot create a Gig in this category without delivering this element in the package.
  • A pricing element you cannot include in this package. It may be available in other packages or as a standalone extra.
  • Your package price must be at or above this amount to keep pricing realistic, maintain the category’s quality standards, and ensure fair competition.
  • We recommend adding this element as an extra to expand your offering and reach more potential clients. In rare cases, adding it may be mandatory to ensure proper pricing for a specific element.

How to set up Gig packages

  • To create or activate packages on your Gig:
    • Go to your Gig’s Pricing section in the Gig create & edit flow.
    • Click the 3 Packages toggle to activate packages mode.
    • Set the scope, revisions, and extras for each package.
    • Add a name, description, pricing, and delivery time for each package.
    • Click Save.
  • If your Gig is in a standardized category:
    • Review the minimum requirements for your category before editing.
    • Update each package to meet all mandatory pricing elements.
    • Fill in all required metadata fields.
    • Save your changes before the deadline.
  • If your Gig does not meet the minimum requirements for its current category, consider moving it to a more relevant one. Missing required fields may reduce your Gig’s visibility in search.

Best practices

  • Naming your packages: Keep package names simple and descriptive. Each name should highlight what makes that tier distinct and stand out to clients who are comparing options.
  • Choosing what to include: Think about the extras clients ask for most often, or the elements that make your Gig deliver the best results. Build each package around those elements and price them accordingly.
  • Staying compliant with standardized requirements: Check your dashboard for notifications about required updates. Complete any required changes within 30 days. If you do not make the required changes within this timeframe, your Gig may lose visibility on the platform.
  • Using custom offers for non-standard requests: Standardized package requirements apply to the package structure only, not to custom offers. If a client has specific needs that your packages do not cover, you can create a custom offer at an agreed price.

FAQs, freelancer

  • You can price packages starting from $5, up to the maximum price for that package tier. We recommend browsing your category to see how other freelancers price comparable packages.

  • No. Packages do not affect your ratings.
  • If your Gig does not meet the minimum requirements for its category, we may reduce its visibility on the platform. You have 30 days to make the required changes. If your Gig does not fit the category’s requirements, consider moving it to a more relevant category.

  • Fiverr sets standardized minimum pricing and service requirements for certain categories. This ensures that every freelancer in that category delivers a consistent level of quality that matches the category’s standards.

Creating Gig images and tagging your Gig gallery

Your Gig gallery is often a client’s first impression of your service, so the images, videos, and tags you choose directly affect the traffic and orders you get. This article explains how to prepare Gig images that meet our guidelines, and how to tag each gallery item so we can show your work to the clients most likely to hire you. Following these guidelines helps you stand out in search results, avoid having your Gig flagged, and attract clients who are a good fit for your service. These guidelines apply to freelancers who offer services through Gigs.

Before you begin

These guidelines apply to your Gig images, and also to your videos and audio thumbnails. Each Gig gallery holds up to three images, one video, and two PDFs. You manage your images and your tags from the Manage Gigs page. Gallery tagging works in selected categories only, and your tag values come from the Gig metadata you select in the Overview tab, so choose your metadata before you start tagging.

If you want help building your Gig image, our Gig image experts are here to help.

Gig image size & quality

Create high-quality Gig images that showcase your services clearly and help you stand out to potential clients.

  • The recommended Gig image size is 1280 x 769 px at 72 dots per inch (DPI).
    • Minimum: 712 x 430 px
    • Maximum: 4000 x 2416 px
  • To resize your Gig images on a Mac, use Preview. On Windows, use Photo Gallery. You can also find other free tools online.
  • For image quality, use sharp, clear, high-resolution, and eye-catching images that stand out to potential clients. Avoid blurry, pixelated, stretched, or squished images.
  • Keep it simple. You can upload up to three images per Gig.

If your image fails to upload or appears broken, export or save it with the metadata removed before uploading. This is especially helpful for images created with AI. Most photo and design tools have an “export without metadata” or “remove metadata” option. If a JPEG upload still doesn’t work, upload the image as a PNG instead.

What to include in your Gig images

Create relevant, original, and visually engaging Gig images that accurately represent your service and capture potential clients’ attention.

  • Your Gig images must directly relate to the service you provide. Random images can damage your Gig’s reputation and lower your chance of an editorial pick. Clickbait or misleading content frustrates potential clients, can lower your ranking in search results, and can damage your Gig’s reputation.
  • Don’t settle for generic visuals. Choose images that spark curiosity, connect emotionally with your target audience, and reflect your unique service. Creative, thoughtful imagery sets the tone and makes your Gig more memorable. If you offer more than one Gig, choose unique images and text for each one.
  • Text overlays can make your Gig image more informative or more eye-catching. Use them sparingly so they don’t overcrowd the image, and avoid repeating text that already appears elsewhere on your Gig card.
    • Keep the text to no more than 10 words.
    • Use fonts that stay easy to read at small sizes.
    • Make sure the text contrasts clearly with the background, either much darker or much lighter.
  • For a more dynamic and informative Gig image, combine custom graphics, real photos, and a small amount of text. Keep the layout clean, and give each element a purpose, whether it showcases your work, highlights a benefit, or guides the viewer’s attention.
  • Give your image file a clear, relevant name. A descriptive file name supports search engine optimization (SEO) and makes your Gig easier to find in search results.
  • We encourage you to use a picture of yourself. Aim for a visually pleasing, easy to understand image that follows Fiverr’s Community Standards.
    • Authenticity: Take a front-facing photo of yourself, and do not misrepresent yourself in any way.
    • Quality: Use a basic, clean background, and make sure the lighting is good so both you and the background are clearly visible. Avoid dark, blurry, or pixelated images.
    • Orientation and size: Use horizontal (landscape) mode, and crop the image to the correct proportions. Use the same dimensions as any other Gig image: 1280 x 769 px at 72 DPI, with a minimum of 712 x 430 px and a maximum of 4000 x 2416 px.
  • These photo guidelines apply to your Gig images only, not to your freelancer profile.

Content rules for Gig images

Make sure your Gig images follow Fiverr’s content standards and only include material you have the right to use.

  • Only use images that you have permission to use.
  • Do not use logos of other companies or platforms without the owner’s consent or the license holder’s permission. Check Fiverr’s Terms of Service for each logo. Keep your images clean and simple rather than crowding them with logos or text.
    • Add up to 10 words of text.
    • Add up to five graphics or logos of relevant platforms, for example social media.
  • We add badges to your Gig automatically, so do not add Fiverr logos, ratings, level badges, or any other badges yourself. If you do, we will flag your Gig and remove it.
  • Never include private information on your Gig images, including contact information. This applies to both your own individual and business details and those of a client. Keep all communication within Fiverr.
  • We do not accept objectionable content, for example adult material or hate speech. Learn more in Fiverr’s Community Standards.
  • Your Gig images must meet Fiverr’s Terms of Service and Fiverr’s Community Standards. If your Gig does not meet these standards, for example because it contains offensive content, adult material, or hate speech, we will remove it.

Gig gallery tagging

Gallery tagging lets you add tags to each item in your Gig gallery, which brings more relevant traffic to your Gig. When you tag your gallery items accurately, we can show your most relevant reviews with files to the clients browsing your Gig, based on what each client is interested in. Clients who find reviews with files that match their needs are more likely to open your Gig and order from it.

You can tag each item in two ways:

  • Choose values from your Gig metadata and apply them to each gallery item.
  • Add free text tags that highlight the unique talent or expertise shown in that item.

Add only keywords that are relevant to the specific gallery item. Non-relevant tags can hurt your Gig and reduce its overall performance, so be as specific as possible when you choose your keywords.

Categories that support gallery tagging

You can tag gallery items in these categories.

  • Graphics & Design: Illustration, Book Design, Album Cover Design, Social Media Design, Presentation Design, Flyer Design, Architecture & Interior Design (including 3D Modeling & Rendering), and Packaging Design
  • Music & Audio: Session Musicians and Voice Over
  • Video & Animation
  • Photography: Product Photographers
How to tag your Gig gallery
  • Go to your Manage Gigs page.
  • Select Edit for the Gig you want to update.
  • Select the Gallery tab.
  • Select Add tags to this sample for the item you want to tag.
  • Choose the tags that apply to that item in the window that opens.

Your tag options come from the Gig metadata you selected in the Overview tab. To make other options available, change that selection.

Best practices for your Gig gallery

A polished, relevant gallery can boost your credibility, attract the right traffic, and increase conversions.

  • Use high-quality visuals that clearly represent your service.
  • Tailor your content to your niche, for example, logo variations for design, code screenshots for development, or resume samples for career services.
  • Show real examples of your work, with permission where needed.
  • Keep it clean and professional, and avoid clutter or off-topic visuals.
  • For videos, explain your process, highlight your strengths, and speak directly to clients. Keep the video short, clear, and engaging.
  • Use smart, relevant tagging to improve your search visibility and help us connect you with the right audience.

FAQs

  • You can add up to three images, one video, and two PDFs.
  • Use 1280 x 769 px at 72 DPI. The minimum is 712 x 430 px and the maximum is 4000 x 2416 px.
  • Yes. Use a front-facing photo with a clean background and clear lighting, in horizontal (landscape) mode, cropped to the correct proportions. These guidelines apply to your Gig image only, not to your freelancer profile.
  • Up to 10 words, in a font that stays readable at small sizes.
  • Only if you have the owner’s consent or the license holder’s permission. You can add up to five graphics or logos of relevant platforms.
  • No. We add badges automatically. If you add them yourself, we will flag your Gig and remove it.
  • Gallery tagging works in selected categories only. If your Gig is in a supported category and you still do not see the tags you want, check the metadata you selected in the Overview tab, since your tag options come from there.
  • Yes. Non-relevant tags can hurt your Gig and reduce its overall performance, so only tag items with keywords that genuinely apply.

Creating your Fiverr intro video

An Intro video is a short video displayed on your profile and Gig pages that helps you introduce yourself to potential clients. By appearing on camera, you can create a more personal connection, build trust, and clearly explain what you offer while helping clients feel more confident choosing you.

What is an Intro video?

An Intro video allows you to present your professional profile and services directly to potential clients.

  • What it does: Displays a short video on your profile and Gig pages.
  • Why it’s useful: Builds a personal connection with clients, increases engagement and helps you clearly communicate your services and unique value.
  • Who it’s for: Freelancers with a level who want to enhance their profile and service presentation

Requirements and guidelines

To be approved, your Intro video must meet the following requirements.

  • Your Intro video should be a personal, professional introduction that helps potential clients understand who you are, what you offer, and what they can expect when working with you.
    • You must personally appear on camera and introduce yourself
    • Do not include other individuals in the video
    • Do not use AI avatars or AI-generated video content
    • Clearly explain the specific services you offer
    • Focus on your relevant skills, experience, expertise, and past work
    • Describe how you approach projects and what clients can expect when working with you
    • Highlight the value you provide and what makes your approach unique
  • Your video should be created specifically as a personal introduction. Showreels, animations, advertisements, or standard explainer videos that do not personally introduce you and your services may not be approved.
  • Your Intro video and everything shown or mentioned in it must comply with Fiverr’s policies.
    • Do not promote services that violate Fiverr’s Community Standards
    • Do not include watermarks, copyrighted material, or other content you do not own or have permission to use
    • Do not make misleading claims or guarantee specific results
    • Do not display Fiverr logos, badges, freelancer levels, or rating stars
    • Do not share personal contact information or ask clients to communicate or complete transactions outside Fiverr
  • Your video should be clear, stable, and easy to watch and understand.
    • Record your video in landscape orientation
    • Keep the camera stable and avoid shaking footage
    • Position yourself frontally, centered in the frame, and at eye level
    • Film in a clean, professional setting using natural daylight (avoid backlighting or overhead lighting)
    • Use suitable lighting so that you are clearly visible
    • Make sure your spoken English is clear and easy to understand
    • If you speak another language, include accurate English subtitles
    • Make sure the audio is synchronized with the video
    • Avoid distortion, background noise, or other sounds that make it difficult to hear you
  • Your video must meet the following technical requirements:
    • Length: 20–60 seconds
    • Minimum resolution: 1280 × 720
    • Maximum file size: 5 GB
    • Language: English, or include English subtitles
  • If your video does not meet these requirements, you’ll receive an error message and will need to update it before resubmitting.

How to upload an Intro video

Follow these steps to add an Intro video to your profile:

  • From your dashboard, select Switch to Selling
  • Click View profile
  • Scroll down and click Add Intro video
  • Upload your video file from your computer
  • Submit the video for review

After uploading, your video will enter moderation and will be published once approved.

Tip: You can replace your Intro video at any time by uploading a new one from your profile page.

Best practices for a professional Intro video

Use the tips below to create a high-quality and effective video:

  • While it’s helpful to plan what you’ll say, aim to sound natural rather than reading directly from a script. Your video should include:
    • Introduction: Greet viewers and introduce yourself
    • Clarity: Briefly explain your services, experience, and specialization
    • Personality: Share what you enjoy about your work
    • Unique value: Mention a skill or detail that differentiates you
    • Call to action: Invite clients to work with you
  • Example:
  • “Hello! I’m {full name}, and I specialize in {gig offering}. With over {years of experience} years of experience in {field}, I focus on delivering high-quality results for my clients.
  • I especially enjoy working on {project types}, where I can bring creativity and attention to detail into every project. What sets me apart is {unique skill or fun fact}.
  • I’d love to help bring your ideas to life, so let’s work together.”
    • Camera: Use a smartphone back camera or any HD-capable digital camera.
    • Camera placement: Position the camera at eye level on a stable surface or tripod.
    • Camera orientation: Film horizontally (landscape mode).
    • Microphone: External microphones or wired headphones can improve audio quality.
    • Choose a clean, professional setting (office or studio)
    • Use natural daylight when possible; avoid backlighting or overhead lighting
    • Dress professionally while reflecting your personality
    • Keep your face clearly visible and make eye contact by speaking directly to the camera as if addressing the client
      • Do not wear hats, sunglasses, or accessories that block your face
  • Avoid the following to ensure your video is approved:
    • Showing other individuals in the video
    • Asking clients to communicate outside Fiverr or sharing personal contact information
    • Displaying Fiverr badges, freelancer levels, or rating stars
    • Including watermarks or copyrighted content you don’t own
    • Offering services that violate Fiverr’s Community Standards

Inspiration and examples

For additional guidance, visit Fiverr’s Community to learn more about creating effective gig visuals and to view Intro video examples from other freelancers.

You can learn more about Creating the perfect gig visuals from Fiverr’s Community. Also, check out these Intro videos for more inspiration:

FAQs

  • Your video must be:
    • 20–60 seconds long.
    • Minimum resolution: 1280x720.
    • File size: Up to 5 GB.
  • If your video does not meet these requirements, you will receive an error message and need to update it before resubmitting.
  • Videos may be rejected if:
    • The freelancer is not visible or not speaking in the video.
    • The video includes Fiverr badges, levels, or watermarks.
    • There is poor lighting, low audio quality, or out-of-sync audio/video.
    • The video is not in English or lacks English subtitles.
  • You can see the specific denial reason on your billboard. After correcting the issue, you can delete and resubmit your video.
  • Intro videos are usually reviewed in up to a week. If your video is pending review for more than a week, you can contact support for escalation.
  • No, freelancers currently cannot select a custom thumbnail. The system automatically generates the thumbnail.
  • Intro videos are not available for Agency pages. If you are an Agency, switch back to your freelancer profile to post and publish an Intro video.

Fiverr’s search and recommendation system (Freelancers: Selling on Fiverr)

Fiverr’s search system connects clients with freelancers by focusing on relevance, client satisfaction, and personalization. Understanding how the system works helps clients find the right talent and helps freelancers understand how their listings are surfaced on the platform. We use a combination of ranking factors, special listing types, and behavioral data to ensure the most relevant results appear for every search.

How search works on Fiverr

Clients can find freelancers in two ways:

  • Category pages: Browse listings organized by service category. These pages show all available services in a specific area of Fiverr’s catalog.
  • Search engine: Enter a text query to see the most relevant matches. The system reads your query, interprets your intent, and shows listings from freelancers whose services match.

Both the Category pages and the Search results page show only listings from freelancers who are currently available to take orders.

Clients can also refine search results using filters, including freelancer language and service-specific requirements.

How search rankings work

Relevancy is the most important ranking factor. The system measures how well a listing’s description matches your search query.

  • Additional ranking factors include:
    • Historical appeal: how attractive the listing has been to clients with similar needs, based on past searches and transactions
    • Client satisfaction: satisfaction scores from completed orders on a particular service
    • Machine learning models, review scores, pricing, availability, and freelancer responsiveness
  • These factors work together to ensure the listings you see are relevant and high quality.
  • Special listing types that may also appear in search results:
    • Fiverr’s Choice: We award this badge to select services in recognition of outstanding quality and client satisfaction.
    • Pro freelancers: The Fiverr Pro team vets these freelancers for quality and expertise. Learn more with How to become a Fiverr Pro freelancer.
    • Fiverr Ads promoted listings: These are Gigs from freelancers who have opted for paid exposure. We verify their relevance and quality before they appear. These Gigs show an ad badge. Learn more with Promoting your Gigs with Fiverr Ads.
    • Pricing diversity: We aim to show a range of pricing options so clients can compare choices.

How we personalize your results

We analyze client behavior and preferences to tailor search results to individual needs. Personalization includes:

  • Adjusting results to match the languages spoken by clients.
  • Prioritizing freelancers who can deliver services quickly when we detect urgency.
  • Using data analytics to align results with individual client behavior on the platform.

If you want to influence the recommendations shown to you, you can block a listing so it no longer appears in your results. This option is available on the platform.

FAQs

  • Yes. You can use Fiverr’s search filters to refine results by freelancer language, service-specific requirements, and more.
  • We award the Fiverr’s Choice badge to select services that demonstrate outstanding quality and client satisfaction.
  • You can block a listing so it no longer appears in your search results or recommendations. This option is available on the platform.
  • Relevancy is the most important factor, determined by how well your listing description matches a client’s search query. Additional factors include historical client interest in similar listings, client satisfaction scores, review scores, pricing, your availability, and your responsiveness.
  • The Fiverr Pro team vets Pro freelancers for quality and expertise. Pro status can influence search ranking.
  • Promoted listings are Gigs from freelancers who have opted for paid exposure. We verify their relevance and quality before they appear. They show an ad badge in search results.

Freelancer dashboard for web and mobile app

In your freelancer profile on Fiverr, you can manage your workload and daily tasks directly from your home screen, which is also known as the dashboard. Utilize your dashboard page to help you organize ongoing projects and grow as a Fiverr freelancer.

I am a new freelancer

Your dashboard is organized to help guide you to realize your full potential on Fiverr.

Features of your dashboard include:

  • This section located at the top of your dashboard provides a quick overview of your account information. See your username, display name, and level status. If you are a member of Seller Plus, you can see your status here as well. Learn more about Fiverr’s level system and Seller Plus Program.
  • Any important information about your account will be shown in a banner under the profile panel.
  • A strong profile helps you stand out and attract new clients! Improve your profile strength score by adding more information about your experience and expertise. Please note that you have the option to add more information about yourself, such as adding a Portfolio and Intro video which is not mandatory.
  • The onboarding steps are designed to help new freelancers get ready to sell on Fiverr. Each task must be completed in order; finishing one step will unlock the next. You’ll need to complete all steps in this section before your profile becomes visible and searchable to clients in the marketplace.
  • Enhance your professional development by exploring the articles and webinars in this section, all designed to help you succeed on Fiverr.

I am an experienced freelancer

Your dashboard is designed to help you manage your workload efficiently and track your progress and earnings on Fiverr.

Features of your dashboard include:

  • This section located at the top of your dashboard provides a quick overview of your account information. See your username, display name, seller level, Seller Plus membership status, and set Availability.
  • Any important information about your account will be shown in a banner under the profile panel.
  • This section can help you manage your workload and prioritize your tasks by showing you in progress orders, unread messages, and briefs. You can choose to filter by order progress status and click into messages to respond directly from the dashboard.
  • A strong profile helps you stand out and attract new clients! Improve your profile strength score by adding more information about your experience and expertise. Please note that you have the option to add more information about yourself, such as adding a Portfolio and Intro video which is recommended but not mandatory.
  • Eligible freelancers are encouraged to add Featured clients and Paid consultations to their profile which will improve your profile strength score.
  • Note that your Profile Strength is optional and not completing the score will not affect your impressions or freelancer metrics.
  • Use this section to understand your achievements and identify areas for improvement on Fiverr. Hover over each icon to view your metrics and earnings, and explore the criteria required to reach the next level. Let’s review what each metric means:
    • My level
    • Success score
    • Rating
    • Response rate
    • Orders: Shows the total number of orders you’ve completed on Fiverr.
    • Unique clients: This metric shows the number of different clients you’ve worked with on Fiverr. (Each client counts once, regardless of how many orders they’ve placed.)
    • Earnings: This metric shows your total earnings on Fiverr.
  • Track your performance by viewing Analytics data right from your dashboard. You can view your Earnings, Success Score, Rating, and Response rate, designed to help you reflect on your achievements.
  • Enhance your professional development by exploring the articles and webinars in this section, all designed to help you succeed on Fiverr.

Mobile dashboard overview

There are 4 sections on the App dashboard. The top section shows the performance metrics related to your level, followed by: Earnings, To-Dos, and My Gigs.

Note: Make sure the ‘Selling’ mode toggle is turned on. This feature is only available on recent app versions: Android: 4.0.5 or later and iOS: 3.34 or later.

  • At the top of the screen, you’ll see the performance metrics that contribute to your level status. If you tap on any area in this section, you will see more details on these metrics: Level, Success Score, Rating, Response rate, Orders, Unique clients and Earnings.
  • In this section, you can see your personal balance, your earnings for the current month, the average selling price for your Gigs, active orders, earnings that have not yet cleared, and canceled orders. Tap to see more details.
  • In this section, you can see activity for any unread messages, revision requests, upcoming deliveries, late deliveries, and new orders. Tap any one for more details.
  • In this section, you can see your Gig statistics for the last 7 days.
  • Let’s review what each Gig statistic means:
    • Impressions: These are the number of times your Gig appeared in the thumbnails (on the homepage, category/subcategory page, search, and user page).
    • Clicks: These are clicks from impressions or the number of clicks after a user saw it once on the homepage, category/subcategory page, search, and user page.
    • Views: These are the number of page views on the actual Gig page.
    • Conversion: This is the total number of orders resulting from clicks after views.

Gigs best practices

A well-crafted Gig is your storefront on Fiverr. These best practices cover everything you need to build a strong profile, write compelling Gig content, price your services, and promote your work to grow your business.

Fiverr policies & guidelines

To keep Fiverr a high-quality and safe marketplace, all members must follow our Community Standards. Here are the key policies to help you and your clients have the best experience.

  • Follow these guidelines to present yourself authentically on Fiverr:
    • Use a profile picture so clients can put a face to your name.
    • Write an accurate description of your professional background.
    • Add your education and skills to showcase your qualifications.
    • Fill out the professional website section for extra credibility with Fiverr’s moderation teams.
  • Follow these guidelines to maintain professional communication on Fiverr:
    • Your services must align with our Terms of Service.
    • Keep all business communication on Fiverr to stay protected and supported.
    • Be polite, send informative updates, and maintain a collaborative relationship with clients.
    • Do not spam members or contact them about anything unrelated to their Gigs or orders.
    • Do not ask clients for positive reviews. The best way to earn a great review is to be responsive, professional, and helpful.
    • Do not discriminate based on gender, religion, ethnicity, or nationality.

Optimizing your Gig content

The right content attracts the right clients. Focus on each of the following areas to make your Gig stand out.

  • Your title appears in search results and creates your first impression. Start with a strong verb after “I will,” use the most relevant keyword, and make sure it is grammatically correct.
  • Browse your subcategory to find the most common keywords for your service, then add the relevant tags to your Gig.
  • Clearly describe what you offer and what sets you apart. Include:
    • The value and skills you bring.
    • Any services you do not provide.
    • Languages, platforms, or software you use (when relevant).
    • Your turnaround time and number of revisions.
  • Avoid repeating information you have already provided in other sections of your Gig.
  • Add FAQs to your Gig so clients know exactly what to expect before ordering. Include the questions you are most frequently asked and any other relevant information clients should know.
  • Use a template in your Gig requirements to save time and set clear expectations. List everything you need from a client to start the order.

Optimizing your Gig gallery

Visuals are often the first thing clients notice. A strong gallery increases click-through rates and helps clients understand your service quickly.

  • Use high-quality, visually appealing Gig images. See our Gig image guidelines for specifications.
  • Add a video showreel to showcase your skills. Gigs with videos perform better.
  • For non-visual services, create a unique image that explains your Gig and attracts clients. Including a photo of yourself can add credibility.
  • After uploading your image, review your Gig card to make sure it looks centered and clear.
  • PDFs with reviews or your resume are good options for written-word content.

Pricing your Gig

When setting your price, consider how long the service takes, what your time is worth, and that your earnings are 80% of the purchased amount.

  • Check the average rate in the marketplace for your service before setting your price.
  • Use Gig Extras to offer additional services for a fee (for example, providing a source file for an extra charge).
  • Use the custom offer feature to create tailored offers for clients with specific needs.
  • Create at least three packages at different price points to capture a wider audience.
  • As your reputation grows, revisit your rates and increase them accordingly.

Promoting your Gig

Once your Gig is optimized, use these tools to increase your visibility and attract more clients.

  • Custom offers: Send personalized offers to clients who need a tailored service.
  • Freelancer badge embed: Add a badge to your personal blog or website that links directly to your profile.
  • Social media share: Share your profile on social media to bring your followers to your Gig.
  • Matching with clients: Use the Fiverr matching feature to find relevant client requests and send offers.

FAQs

  • Use the most relevant keyword in your Gig title and add search tags that match what clients look for in your subcategory. Browse similar Gigs to see which terms appear most often, then apply them to your own.
  • Yes. You can create up to three packages at different price points to appeal to a wider range of clients. You can also use Gig Extras to offer add-ons, or send a custom offer for clients with specific needs.
  • Add at least one high-quality image that clearly represents your service. If possible, include a short video showcasing your work, as Gigs with videos tend to perform better. For written-word services, a PDF with samples or reviews is a good option.

Glossary of Fiverr terms (Freelancers: Selling on Fiverr)

This glossary defines common terms you will come across on Fiverr, so you always know what a feature, program, or process means. Understanding these terms helps you use Fiverr’s tools with confidence, whether you are ordering a service or offering one. Terms are grouped by audience, clients first and then freelancers, with links to related articles for more detail.

Terms for clients

  • Agencies consist of a multi-skilled team of people who can offer a wider range of services and handle more complex, large-scale projects. An agency is a type of user account designed for teams rather than individual freelancers.

  • You can request to cancel an active order through the Resolution Center when issues arise. Once you send a cancellation request, the freelancer has 48 hours to accept or decline it. If the freelancer does not respond in that time, we cancel the order automatically. You can cancel without the freelancer’s approval if they never submitted your requirements or if delivery is more than 24 hours overdue.
  • Related article: How cancellations work for clients
  • Our Community Standards form a living framework that helps us maintain a marketplace that is respectful, inclusive, and safe for everyone. They protect your safety, your work, and your creative expression, and help keep the marketplace fair and trusted.
  • Related article: Our Community Standards
  • Custom offers are personalized orders freelancers send directly to clients to match specific needs not covered by standard gig packages. To get started, message a freelancer and request a custom offer.
  • Related article: Paying for orders, extras, or custom offers
  • When a freelancer completes an order, they deliver the final work, such as a spreadsheet, a logo, or a video, to the client. An order can include one or more deliverables, sent in a single delivery or across multiple deliveries. The order is complete once the client approves the final delivery. Make sure not to accept a delivery unless you are fully happy with the work.
  • Related article:The complete guide to your Fiverr order: Statuses and process
  • Extras are optional add-ons that freelancers can offer with their services, such as faster delivery, commercial rights, or specific customizations. You can add one or more extras when you place your order.
  • Related article: Paying for orders, extras, or custom offers
  • We give the Fiverr’s Choice badge to select services in recognition of outstanding quality and client satisfaction.
  • Related article: Fiverr’s search and recommendation system
  • A freelancer on Fiverr is a registered user who offers services to clients.
  • Freelancers can reach different levels, Level 1, Level 2, and Top Rated, by meeting specific performance criteria linked to their work on the platform and their relationship with clients.
  • Related article: Understanding Fiverr’s freelancer levels
  • A gig is the service listing a freelancer creates to show their skills, packages, and reviews to potential clients. Most freelancers offer up to three gig packages, Basic, Standard, and Premium, each at a different price and with different inclusions. When you find a gig that matches your needs, you can order it directly or request a custom offer.
  • Related article: How Fiverr works for clients
  • Some freelancers offer milestones for their larger, more complex services. Each milestone represents a separate task in the freelancer’s workflow, with its own deadline, delivery, and payment.
