These consultations can increase your confidence in choosing the right freelancer and set the stage for a successful collaboration.
  • Related article:Consultations for clients
  • We rigorously vet Pro freelancers for expertise in their field, high ratings, and quality of work. When you order from a Fiverr Pro freelancer, you work with vetted, professional talent.
  • Related article: Fiverr Pro freelancer: Badge and benefits
  • When we cancel an order, we credit the funds to your Fiverr balance by default. Once we approve your cancellation request, you can request a refund to your original payment method from the Available balances tab. Refunds to your payment provider can take up to 10 days to process.
  • Related article: Refunds
  • On some gigs, a freelancer may require you to send a request to order before you can place your order. This gives you the chance to discuss your project’s specific requirements, confirm the right package, and align on details and timelines before committing. Request to order is not available on all gigs.
  • Related article: How Fiverr works for clients
  • The Resolution Center is a resource available to both clients and freelancers to help resolve order issues. We recommend using the Resolution Center to work out any issues before you contact Customer Support.
  • Related article: Using the Resolution Center
  • We use a two-way review system: both you and the freelancer can leave a review after an order is completed. A public review is a star rating plus written feedback that appears on the freelancer’s gig page and profile. A private review is an anonymous satisfaction rating that we use for internal quality measurement only, and it is not shared with the freelancer. Public reviews become visible only after both parties submit their feedback, or once the review window closes.
  • Related article: Leaving and managing reviews on Fiverr
  • Freelancers can offer a set number of revisions with each service, giving you the ability to request changes to your order before you approve the final delivery. Some services offer additional revisions as an extra. Not all services include or offer revisions, so talk with your freelancer beforehand.
  • Related article: Managing your orders: A freelancer’s guide to the Fiverr order process
  • Each service a freelancer offers has a scope, set deliverables, and fixed pricing. Freelancers can create different packages for each service and offer optional extras. If an existing service matches your needs, you can order it directly. You can find services on various pages of the site and through the search bar, with the search toggle set to Services. For more customized needs, you can work with a freelancer on a custom offer.
  • Related article: How Fiverr works for clients
  • Subscriptions let you work with your favorite freelancers on an ongoing basis, ideal for repeat orders. Subscriptions are only available in certain subcategories and can only be offered by select freelancers.
  • Related article: Subscriptions

Terms for freelancers

  • If you are planning to be out of town, are overbooked, or just need time off, you can schedule the dates you will be unavailable directly from your profile. On the mobile app, tap Availability in the main menu. While you are unavailable, your gigs stay hidden and you will not receive new orders, though you can still message clients with active orders.
  • Related article: Setting your availability
  • Often, clients have projects with specific needs that require personalized solutions. For these clients, you can create custom offers to meet their needs. Requests for custom offers are sometimes called “getting a quote.”
  • Related article: Creating and managing custom offers
  • Your dashboard is the central hub for your freelancer activity, giving you an at-a-glance view of your earnings, orders, freelancer level, and inbox.
  • Related article: Freelancer dashboard for web and mobile app
  • The freelancer level system offers transparent metrics that show exactly what drives your progress. As you advance to higher levels, Level 1, Level 2, and Top Rated, you gain new benefits and tools. Each level has its own criteria across six performance metrics: success score, rating, response rate, orders, unique buyers, and earnings. You need an additional evaluation to qualify for Top Rated.
  • Related articles: Understanding Fiverr’s freelancer levels and Everything you need to know about response time and rate
  • Fiverr’s Freelancer Rewards Program rewards certain high-performing freelancers with a cash bonus based on their annual earnings growth on Fiverr.
  • Related article: Fiverr’s Freelancer Reward Program
  • The live portfolio feature lets you share client-approved samples of work you have completed on Fiverr. When you enable live portfolio on a gig, we add these samples to both the gig gallery and your portfolio.
  • Related article:Using your Fiverr Portfolio
  • With Fiverr Ads, you can run ads on the Fiverr marketplace to increase the visibility of your services and professions. Ad placements include prime locations in search results, category pages, and the inbox. You control your daily budget and how much you are willing to pay per click. This program is only available to freelancers who are Level 1 or higher.
  • Related article: Promoting your Gigs with Fiverr Ads
  • Response rate is the percentage of first responses to new messages you send within 24 hours, tracked over the last 90 days. Response time is the average number of hours it takes you to respond to a new message in your inbox. Your response rate is visible only to you, while clients can see your response time.
  • Related article: Everything you need to know about response time and rate
  • You can add revisions when you create a new service, so clients can give feedback on deliveries and get exactly what they need.
  • Related articles: Revisions and Revisions done right
  • Seller Plus is a paid membership program that helps freelancers grow their business on Fiverr. The program offers two tiers, Standard and Premium, each with benefits to support your success on the platform. The Seller Plus program is available by invitation only.
  • Related article: Seller Plus Standard and Premium: Advanced tools for business growth
  • Your success score looks at your order history in key areas related to the order process and your relationship with clients. This score is one of several elements that contribute to your visibility in the marketplace, and it is one of six performance metrics that determine your eligibility for each freelancer level. You can find your success score on your level overview page.
  • Related article: Success score

How Fiverr works for freelancers

Fiverr empowers individuals to transform their talents into thriving businesses by offering freelancers a unique platform to showcase their expertise and connect with a global audience of potential clients. This guide outlines the key principles and best practices every freelancer should follow to launch and scale a successful career on Fiverr.

Before you begin

To ensure a trustworthy platform for everyone, future Fiverr freelancers should be aware of some essential account information before creating a profile.

  • Eligibility: Fiverr’s Minors Policy requires that all users be at least 18 years of age and of legal age to form a binding contract. Users under 18 and at least 13 years of age are permitted to use the site only through an account owned by their parent or legal guardian.
  • Allowed services: Do not offer services that infringe on Fiverr TOS or 3rd parties TOS. Learn more about our Community standards and prohibited services.
Your growth journey on Fiverr

Your journey as a freelancer follows a clear path focused on expertise and service quality.

  • Building your freelancer profile is your gateway to the Fiverr community; professionalism fosters trust and draws in clients.
    • Profile details: As your profile is your window to the Fiverr community, ensure it is complete, error-free, and accurately reflects your expertise to attract customers. Highlight your personal touch by including a professional headshot, clear service descriptions, and specific details about your experiences. Start by creating your freelancer profile to showcase your professional brand.
    • Intro video: Introduce yourself and build credibility with new clients. By featuring yourself on camera in an Intro video.
    • Creating a Gig: On our marketplace, your Gigs (offered services) showcase your talent and provide the information clients need to place an order. To succeed, ensure your Gigs clearly outline service benefits and expectations through high-quality descriptions and clear pricing. Learn all about the Gig creation process with this article.
    • ID Verification: Complete your ID verification to access additional opportunities and start building trust with clients.
    • Add your Portfolio: Set yourself apart and impress potential clients by showcasing two types of work: projects and reviews with files in your Portfolio.
  • Once your Gigs are live, focus on increasing your reach and attracting the right buyers.
    • Understand impressions: In the Fiverr marketplace, “impressions” represent how many times your Gig was seen by potential clients. High impressions are the first step toward clicks which then generates orders. Continuously monitor your Analytics to see how your visibility grows over time.
    • Be active: Staying online and responding quickly to inquiries can naturally boost your visibility in the marketplace. Utilize Quick responses to reply to clients faster and more easily.
    • Utilize Fiverr Ads: Fiverr Ads allows you to promote your Gigs at the top of search results and category pages. You only pay when a potential client clicks on your ad (Cost-per-click), ensuring your budget is spent on actual interest.
  • Managing orders effectively is crucial for long-term success.
    • Order management: Keep your orders on track and ensure a smooth experience for both you and your customers. Learn how in the Managing orders article.
    • Earnings: After an order is completed, freelancers receive 80% of the client’s cleared payment. Funds are subject to a 14-day clearing period before they become available for withdrawal. Eligible programs, such as Top Rated or Fiverr Pro benefit from a shorter clearing period. Learn more with the Withdraw your earnings article.
    • Resolution center: Utilize Fiverr’s Resolution Center to resolve disputes and manage orders with ease.
  • Freelancers can reach different levels by meeting specific performance criteria linked to their work on the platform and their relationships with customers.
    • Fiverr’s leveling system: Each Freelancer level unlocks new benefits and opportunities, with level badges displayed on Gig cards and profiles.
    • Success Score: The Success score is a metric designed to provide you a more accurate reflection of your long-term performance and gives a comprehensive evaluation of your Gig performance based on client satisfaction, communication, and other key order metrics.
    • Fiverr Pro: This is the highest tier of the marketplace, exclusively featuring hand-vetted, best-in-class talent for high-profile clients. Fiverr Pro sellers benefit from priority support and increased visibility.

Best practices

Review these tips to maintain a high-quality reputation and service.

  • Be clear & patient: Guiding new customers through Fiverr’s nuances strengthens their understanding and empowers them to become valuable long-term partners.
  • Be proactive: Treat every order as a golden opportunity. Proactivity setting clear expectations for deliveries and revisions lays the foundation for long-term success, fostering loyalty and positive reviews.
  • Prioritize customer satisfaction: Cultivating customer loyalty goes beyond first impressions. Delivering high-quality service, setting clear expectations, and patiently supporting clients is the foundation for repeat business.
  • Update your status: Use your availability settings and messaging tools to communicate when you are online or unavailable.
  • Promote your services: Gain enhanced visibility in prime locations to reach more clients by using Fiverr Ads.
  • Connect and learn more: Join the Fiverr Community to take part in freelancing discussions, ask questions, get support, and connect with other freelancers.

New freelancers can benefit from Seller Plus Kickstart. This program provides essential tools, expert guidance, and key features to help you understand the Fiverr marketplace, grow your first orders, and successfully launch your freelance business.

FAQ’s

  • Customer Support will never ask you for your password, but they may ask you for your security question’s answer in specific situations (e.g., to verify account ownership). This is always managed through an official Customer Support request.
  • Here is what you need to know about your password and security:
    • Never give out your password
    • Now and again we may ask for a few things from you, but keep in mind:
      • We will never ask you by email, messages, or comments to provide us with your password or sign-in credentials.
      • We will never ask you to email us your password.
      • We will never prompt you to log into a site outside of the fiverr.com domain, nor to download and install an application.
      • Please never download or run such applications or email attachments, since Fiverr will never send these.
  • For additional help regarding policies and safety, please contact our Customer Support specialists using the Contact us tab at the bottom of the page.
  • From time to time, we reach out to the Fiverr community.
  • After the order is marked as complete, you have 14 days to withdraw your funds. A shorter withdrawal period may vary for Top Rated, Seller Plus, Fiverr Pro, or other eligible programs.
  • For an order to be marked as complete:
    • Freelancers must fulfill their orders as described in their Gig description and must deliver completed files and/or proof of work using the Deliver your order button (located on the order page).
    • The client has three days to respond and post a review (or 14 days for gigs with shipping). If no response is provided within the response time, the order will be considered completed.
  • Each payout method has its own specifications for withdrawing.
  • Learn more with Payout methods.
  • Your Fiverr profile can be associated with only one account from each Fiverr withdrawal provider (payout method). This means you cannot have the same PayPal, Payoneer, or any other withdrawal method for two Fiverr accounts. For example, you can have PayPal and Bank Transfer, but you cannot have Bank Transfer and Fiverr revenue card as they are both provided by Payoneer.
  • Withdrawals are final and can’t be undone. We won’t be able to refund or change this process once it has begun.
  • It is the sole responsibility of freelancers to verify their personal tax obligation, report, and pay taxes according to the laws of the state and/or country of residence, as applicable and required by local law and regulations.
  • To communicate with a client, an order needs to be placed which will create a “conversation” thread and you will be able to communicate with the client. You may also contact the client without an order being placed, if the client contacts you first.
  • Uploading files can sometimes fail for various reasons. Please check the following before asking for further assistance:
    • Make sure your flash is up to date on your computer
    • Flash normally updates automatically for most modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox) but may still have limitations in older versions of modern browsers (Internet Explorer).
    • Disable pop-up blockers for Fiverr.com or allow uploads/downloads through your Firewall/Anti-Virus protector from Fiverr.com
    • Make sure your image is a JPEG or PNG
    • Clear your cookies for Fiverr.com
    • Sometimes cookies can hold on to a “session” where your browser thinks it’s still loading an image file. Refreshing your page helps clear the session, but in most cases, clearing your cookies helps.
  • Yes. There is a partial refund option that is available so you can make the necessary payment adjustments to your existing order. The freelancer is the only one who can suggest or initiate a partial refund through the Resolution Center.
  • Learn more with Partial refunds.
  • You can accept a tip. However, it’s advised not to ask for one. Do your best as a freelancer because ultimately it’s up to the client whether to leave a tip or not.
  • Learn more with our Communication tips for orders webinar.

How to verify your personal and business information

At Fiverr, we require all freelancers to verify their personal or business information to maintain marketplace integrity, reduce fraud, and meet regulatory requirements such as the EU Digital Services Act (DSA). This process helps protect your account, prevents fraud, and maintains your ability to work with European Union clients. By verifying your identity, you gain access to our full range of features and can expand your business while contributing to a secure and reliable community. Even if you are already ID verified, you must clarify your status within the personal and business verification process.

Accessing the verification process

  • As a new freelancer, after creating your freelancer profile and before publishing your first Gig, you’ll be required to complete the verification process.
  • If you’re an existing freelancer, you can start the process by navigating to your profile image, selecting Settings > Personal & Business Info > Identity Verification, and clicking the Verify button.

Choosing your status

Once you follow the steps to start the identity verification process, you’ll be prompted to select how you plan to use Fiverr by choosing between two options:

  • Outside of my primary job or profession
  • As part of my primary job or profession

After making your selection, click Next to proceed.

This self-declared status will determine whether you need further verification under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA) or other regulations. If you are unsure which status applies, consider consulting a legal professional.

Freelancers with an active Team Account must verify as traders in accordance with the EU Digital Services Act, and will not have the option to declare they use Fiverr outside of their primary job or profession.

Outside of my primary job or profession

This option indicates that you plan to use Fiverr as a secondary activity, separate from your main job or profession.

  • Verify your phone number.
  • Add a security question.

Once these steps are completed, your verification process for this status is done.

As part of my primary job or profession

This option indicates that Fiverr is a significant part of your professional work. After selecting this option, you will be asked whether your business is registered:

  • No (Individual Trader)
  • Yes, and I’m the sole employee (Sole Trader)
  • Yes, and I have at least 1 employee (Business Trader)

After your information is verified, EU consumers may have access to certain details as required by the DSA regulation. These may include your name, address, email, phone number, and business registration number (if applicable).

After making your selection, follow the steps below based on your chosen status.

If you select “No” or “Yes, and I’m the sole employee”
  • Phone verification.
  • Provide personal information.
  • ID verification.
If you select “Yes, and I have at least one employee”
  • Phone verification.
  • Provide business information.
  • Proof of business verification.
  • ID verification.

Troubleshooting tips

Prepare your ID and documents in advance
  • To complete the verification process successfully, please disable any VPN during verification.
  • Having your original ID (passport, driver’s license, etc.) and any business documents ready will speed up the process.
  • Confirm the ID complies with template and federal requirements and is clearly identifiable.
  • Take a photo of your original ID. Don’t use a saved image, screenshot, or photo taken from another screen.
  • Make sure to upload a valid ID (not expired) that matches the available and selected type.
  • Upload a clear photo of your ID where all information is visible and easily readable.
Double-check all details
  • Make sure your name, address, and any business information exactly match your official documents. Discrepancies may lead to verification failure.
  • Enter the Business ID number and type it in the correct format, as it was assigned to your business by the local government. If you’re unsure, please consult your legal consultant.
  • When filling out forms, provide your details in English, exactly as they appear on your government-issued ID. Use documents with English text when available.
  • Check out our article Business Registration Number Information by Country for detailed guidance on business registration numbers.

Managing Gig extras, source files, and shipping

Gig extras let you offer additional services beyond your base packages, so you can earn more and give clients more choices. You can add extras like fast delivery, extra revisions, source files, and shipping costs directly from the Pricing tab when editing your Gig. This article explains how each type of extra works and how to set it up.

Before you begin

  • You must be a registered freelancer with at least one active Gig to add extras.
  • Gig creation and publishing are not supported on phones or tablets; desktop or laptop only.

How Gig extras work

Gig extras are optional add-ons that clients can purchase alongside your base package. They let you show clients the full range of services you offer without changing your core package prices. Each extra has its own price and, where applicable, its own delivery time.

The three main types of extras are:

  • Fast delivery: Gives the client the option to receive their order faster than the original delivery time in the purchased package.
  • Revisions: Lets you offer additional revisions at an extra cost. This also helps set clear expectations and limits on how many revisions you provide.
  • Additional extras: Any other service related to your specific offering. These increase the order value while providing more value for the client.

How to add Gig extras

  1. Go to your Gigs tab.

  2. Click Edit on the Gig you want to update.

  3. Go to the Pricing tab.

  4. Add the extras you want to offer and set the price for each one.

  5. Click Save.

You can add Gig extras when preparing a custom offer or after the order is live.

Offering source files

When you create your Gig, you can offer source files as an extra. We recommend uploading source files with every delivery, even if the client did not purchase the source file extra. If a client did not select it, the source files will be offered for sale when you deliver the order.

If a client purchases the source file extra, you must upload the source files when you deliver the order.

How to turn on the source file extra
  • In your Gig’s Extras section, mark the checkbox next to Source file extra. Once a client purchases this extra, it appears on the order page.
  • On the order page, go to Deliver your order and click Deliver now. If your work is not ready, select Save draft.
  • To attach your completed work, select Upload work.
  • To attach your source files, select Upload source files. You can upload files up to 5GB.
  • In the Describe what you’ve done section, briefly describe your delivery and click Deliver work. If the client requests revisions, click Redeliver now to access the Deliver modified work button.

Offering shipping for physical Gigs

Some services on Fiverr require physical delivery, such as arts and crafts or collectibles. For these Gigs, you need to include a flat-rate shipping fee that covers both local and international shipping. You add this fee directly into your package prices.

How to include shipping costs in your Gig packages
  • Go to your Gigs that include shipping and click Edit Gig.
  • Go to the Pricing tab.
  • In the Shipping section, unselect the current shipping option.
  • In the Packages table, do the following:
    • Select Shipping to indicate that your Gig price includes shipping.
    • Update your package Price to include a flat-rate shipping fee.
    • If needed, update Delivery Time.
  • Click Save.
Important information about shipping
  • Clients must provide a shipping address. Make sure all shipping information, including the address, is correct before you deliver.
  • We do not handle or guarantee shipping, tracking, quality, condition, or delivery of shipped items.
  • We are not responsible or liable for any damages or other problems resulting from shipping.
  • We recommend entering a tracking number on the order page when delivering a shipped Gig. A tracking number helps avoid disputes.
  • For shipped Gigs, once you deliver an item, the client has 14 days to respond and post a review.

FAQs

  • Yes. You can add extras to any active Gig from the Pricing tab. Fast delivery and revisions are available across all categories. Source file extras are available in specific categories only.
  • You can still upload source files when you deliver the order. They will be offered for sale to the client at that point. We recommend uploading source files with every delivery.
  • No. We do not handle or guarantee shipping, tracking, quality, condition, or delivery of shipped items. We are also not responsible for any damages or problems resulting from shipping. You are responsible for all shipping arrangements.
  • Update your package prices to include a flat-rate shipping fee that covers both local and international shipping. Do this in the Packages table under the Pricing tab.
  • After you deliver a shipped Gig, the client has 14 days to respond and leave a review.

Managing your Gigs

The Gig management page is your central hub for viewing, updating, and tracking all your Gigs on Fiverr. You can monitor performance, control your order flow, and keep your services running smoothly. This article explains how to manage your Gig statuses, read your statistics, and use the limit orders in queue feature.

Before you begin

  • Go to My Business > Gigs from the top navigation to access the Gig management page.
  • Gig statistics are not available on the Fiverr app. Use a desktop browser to view them.

Gig statuses

On the Gig management page, you can view your Gigs by status. For each Gig, you can also see the total number of impressions, clicks, orders, and cancellations. If a Gig is eligible for Subscriptions, the Plans area will show you the option to manage them.

Your Gig can have one of the following statuses:

  • Active: Your Gig is live and visible in the marketplace.
  • Pending Approval: Your Gig is under review.
  • Requires Modification: Your Gig requires edits before it can be published. If it requires edits, additional information on what needs to be changed is shared under this status.
  • Draft: Your Gig has not been published yet.
  • Denied: Your Gig was not approved. You can view the reason on the Gig management page.
  • Paused: Your Gig is not currently visible to clients, but you can reactivate it.
Available actions by Gig status

Depending on the status of your Gig, you can take the following actions:

  • Preview
  • Edit
  • Pause
  • Activate
  • Share
  • Delete
  • Add Video
  • Manage Live Portfolio
Denied Gigs

If your Gig is denied, you will see an alert at the top of the Gig management page. Click click here in the alert to go to the Denied Gigs section. There, hover over the exclamation mark icon to see a short explanation, or click the Gig to expand the section and view the full reason.

Gig actions

  • To create a new Gig, click the Create a new Gig button on the Gig management page.
  • Learn the step-by-step process with Creating a Gig.
  • The number of active Gigs you can have at one time depends on your freelancer level:
  • Level
  • Active Gig limit
  • New freelancer
  • 4
  • Level 1
  • 10
  • Level 2
  • 10
  • Top Rated
  • 30
  • If you reach your active Gig limit, you will see a banner on the Gig management page. You will not be able to create new Gigs or unpause existing ones until you are within your limit.
  • Gigs created before your current level will not be automatically deleted or paused, even if your level changes and they exceed the current limit for it.
  • Follow these steps to edit your Gig:
    • Go to My Business > Gigs.
    • Find the Gig you want to update and click the arrow to the right of it.
    • Select Edit.
    • Make your changes across any of the tabs: Overview, Pricing, Description, Requirements, Gallery, and others.
    • Save your changes.
  • Significant edits, such as changes to the title, category, or pricing, may trigger a review. Your Gig may not be visible until the review is complete. If you change your Gig title, the URL link will remain with the old one as that cannot be changed.
  • Follow these steps to pause or activate your Gig:
    • Go to My Business > Gigs.
    • Find the Gig you want to manage and click the arrow to the right of it.
    • Select Pause or Activate.
  • Follow these steps to delete your Gig:
    • Go to My Business > Gigs.
    • Find the Gig you want to remove and click the arrow to the right of it.
    • Select Delete.
  • Follow these steps to translate your Gig:
    • Go to My Business > Gigs.
    • Select the Gig you want to translate and click the arrow to the right of it.
    • Select Edit Translation.
    • Edit the fields for your Gig title, description, FAQs, price packages, and gallery details.
    • Save your changes.
  • Completed translations go through an approval and review process. A notification will appear when the review is done.

Gig Summary feature

Gig Summary is an AI-generated overview that appears at the top of your Gig page, giving potential clients a quick, structured snapshot of what you offer.

  • This feature is rolling out gradually and will be automatically enabled for managed Seller Plus Premium freelancers on eligible Gigs. Gig’s eligibility is based on Gig activity and the freelancer’s history.
  • Gig Summary is designed to help your Gig perform better by improving the experience for potential clients browsing your page, and increasing your visibility in search engines and AI-powered search results.
  • You can enable or disable Gig Summary at any time from your freelancer account:
    • Go to My Business.
    • Select Gigs and click Edit on the relevant Gig.
    • Open Advanced Settings.
    • Scroll down and check or uncheck the Gig Summary option.

Gig Summary is generated by AI, and while we aim for accuracy, errors can occasionally occur. If anything in your Gig Summary seems incorrect or doesn’t reflect your services well, please reach out to our Support team.

Viewing Gig statistics

Each Gig has its own statistics dashboard. Clicking a Gig opens a view that shows your performance data, Gig status, Gig info, and controls for limit orders in the queue, and activates the watermark.

The Fiverr app shows limited Gig statistics. Use a desktop browser to view them in full.

How to view Gig statistics
  • Go to My Business > Gigs.
  • Click on a Gig title to open its statistics dashboard.
  • Scroll down to view your statistics.
  • To view statistics in graph form, scroll to the performance graph and select the statistic you want to display.
Understanding your Gig statistics

The following statistics are available on your Gig page:

  • Impressions are the number of times your Gig appeared in Fiverr thumbnails, including on the homepage, category, and subcategory pages, search results, and user profile pages.
  • Clicks are the number of times a user clicked on your Gig after seeing it on the homepage, a category or subcategory page, search results, or a user profile page.
  • Orders show the total number of orders placed for this Gig.
  • The cancellation rate is the number of all types of canceled orders divided by the total number of orders for this Gig.
  • Subscriptions show the current active subscriptions associated with your Gig.
  • The conversion rate is calculated by dividing the total number of orders by the total number of impressions for this Gig.
  • Gig info shows your average delivery time and the current number of orders in the queue.
  • The Gig performance graph shows your statistics over the last 30 days. You can select the statistic you want to view:
    • Impressions
    • Clicks
    • Orders
    • Conversion rate

How to use watermarks

The Activate Watermark feature adds a Fiverr watermark to your image deliveries so clients can preview your work without being able to use it before the order is completed. The watermark is automatically enabled when you create a Gig.

How to turn the watermark on or off
  • Go to My Business > Gigs.
  • Click on a Gig title.
  • Click the Activate watermark slider to turn the feature on or off.
Where the watermark is applied

The watermark appears on the following file types in your delivery message while the order is active:

  • JPG and JPEG
  • TIFF
  • BMP
  • PNG
  • PDF files in the portfolio slideshow
  • Work Samples
Where the watermark is not applied

The watermark does not appear on:

  • Files sent through the inbox or order page messages
  • Deliveries on completed orders
  • Gig Gallery images
  • Files inside ZIP archives
  • PDF files when opened in fullscreen mode
Watermark on milestone orders

On milestone orders, the watermark is only removed once the entire order is completed. If a milestone is stopped or canceled while a previous one is completed, the watermark is lifted because the order is finalized.

Watermark on mobile

The watermark is visible on both the iOS and Android apps. However, you cannot turn the watermark on or off through the mobile app. Use a desktop browser to manage this setting.

Limiting orders in queue

The limit orders in queue feature lets you control how many orders you take on at one time. Once you reach your set limit, your Gig is temporarily removed from Fiverr search so new clients cannot find it.

You can also enable Keep Direct Link Active, which allows anyone with a direct link to your Gig, such as returning clients, to still place an order even after your limit is reached.

Using this feature does not affect your ranking or ratings.

How to set a limit on orders in queue
  • Go to My Business > Gigs and click on the Gig you want to manage.
  • Scroll to the Limit orders in queue toggle and click it to activate the feature. The toggle turns green when active.
  • Enter the maximum number of orders you want in your queue at one time.
  • Save your settings.

Set your limit to a number of orders you can handle successfully. If you turn off this feature, your Gig will return to search results approximately 15 minutes later.

FAQs

  • Yes. Go to My Business > Gigs, click the arrow next to the Gig, and select Pause. When you are ready to accept orders again, select Activate using the same steps.
  • Significant changes, such as edits to the title, category, or pricing, may trigger a review. Your Gig may not be visible during this time. This is a normal part of our process.
  • You will see a banner on the Gig management page. You will not be able to create new Gigs or unpause existing ones until you are within your limit. Gigs created before the current limits were introduced will not be automatically deleted or paused.
  • Once your limit is reached, your Gig is removed from search. If you enable Keep Direct Link Active, clients with a direct link can still place an order.
  • Your Gig will return to search results approximately 15 minutes after you disable the feature.
  • Statistics are displayed for the past 30 days by default.
  • An impression is counted each time your Gig appears in a thumbnail on the homepage, search results, or a category page. A click is counted when a user opens your Gig by clicking on it from one of those locations.
  • The conversion rate shows how often impressions turn into orders. It is calculated by dividing the total number of orders by the total number of impressions for your Gig.
  • No. Using this feature does not affect your ranking or ratings.
  • The watermark is applied to JPG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, and PNG files in your delivery message while the order is active.
  • No. The watermark only appears on files in the delivery message of an active order. Files sent through inbox or order page messages are not watermarked.
  • The watermark is removed once the order is completed. On milestone orders, it is only removed when the entire order is completed, not after individual milestones.
  • No. You can view the watermark on the iOS and Android apps, but you can only turn it on or off from a desktop browser.
  • Yes. The watermark feature is automatically enabled when you create a Gig. You can turn it off at any time from your Gig statistics page.

Promoting your Gigs outside of Fiverr

Fiverr works hard to get your Gigs in front of clients, through search, category pages, recommendations, and editorial features. But there is also real value in bringing traffic to your profile and Gigs from outside the platform. This article covers the main ways to do it, in line with Fiverr’s Terms of Service.

A note on using AI in your marketing

Fiverr encourages using AI tools ethically and transparently as part of your workflow. You’ll find a short AI tip in each section below. Any task you prefer to outsource can also be purchased from a specialist freelancer on Fiverr. Never use AI to create fake reviews, misleading content, or deepfakes - this violates Fiverr’s Community Standards.

Why promote Gigs outside of Fiverr?

Off-platform advertising means promoting your Fiverr Gigs or profile through channels you own or participate in outside of Fiverr, including social media, websites, newsletters, paid ads, and more. When done well, it complements the organic visibility Fiverr already provides, helps you build a recognizable personal brand, and grows your business over time.

No matter where you promote your Gigs, always point your audience back to your Fiverr profile and conduct all client conversations on the platform. See Fiverr’s off-platform policy for full guidance.

Before you begin

  • Make sure your Fiverr profile is complete and your Gigs are polished before driving external traffic to them.
  • Find your shareable URL: Go to your Gig or profile page and copy the URL from your browser - your profile link is typically in the format “www.fiverr.com/your_username”.
  • On the Fiverr app, use the Share button on any Gig or profile page.
  • Decide which one or two channels you want to start with- it is better to do a small number of things well than to spread yourself thin.

Ways to promote your Gigs outside of Fiverr

  • Create a dedicated account for your Fiverr business on one or two platforms where your ideal clients spend time.
    • Participate authentically in relevant communities and always link back to your Fiverr profile or Gig.
    • AI tip: Draft captions and brainstorm post ideas with an AI writing tool, then edit to match your own voice.
  • A personal website lets you showcase your portfolio and link clients to your Fiverr Gigs.
    • Blog posts on topics in your field help you get found in search engines and build authority in your category.
    • You do not need to build from scratch. Simple portfolio platforms and link-in-bio tools work well. You can also hire a freelancer on Fiverr to help design and build your site.
    • AI tip: Use AI to outline blog posts and research SEO keywords, then write the content yourself. Vibe coding tools can help you build a site quickly, or hire a developer on Fiverr.
  • Forums, Facebook groups, Reddit, and LinkedIn groups are full of potential clients.
    • Be genuinely helpful first, and earn the right to mention your services over time.
    • Always read community rules before posting anything promotional.
    • AI tip: Use AI to help structure a helpful reply to a question you can genuinely answer, then review and edit before posting.
  • Facebook ads, Instagram ads, Google ads, and web banners can drive targeted traffic to your Gigs.
    • Use accurate, high-quality visuals and always send traffic to your Fiverr profile or Gig page.
    • Organic channels are usually a better first step for newer freelancers.
    • AI tip: Generate multiple ad copy variations with AI and A/B test them, or hire a digital marketing freelancer on Fiverr.
  • Writing guest posts, appearing on podcasts, or collaborating with freelancers in complementary fields reaches new audiences and builds lasting credibility.
    • Include a link to your Fiverr profile in every guest contribution.
    • AI tip: Use AI to draft outreach emails and repurpose published content into social posts or a newsletter excerpt.

Best practices

  • Always send traffic to Fiverr. Never share personal contact information in external promotion.
  • Polish your Gigs before driving external traffic.
  • Focus on one or two channels at a time.
  • Use AI to work faster, not to replace your voice. Final content should reflect your genuine expertise.
  • Never use AI to fabricate reviews, testimonials, or engagement.
  • Track what works using source tracking on your social platforms.

FAQs

  • Yes. Sharing a link to your Gig or profile is encouraged. Make sure all calls-to-action point to Fiverr and never share personal contact information.
  • No. Fiverr’s Terms of Service require all communication to happen on the platform.
  • Yes. Fiverr encourages the responsible use of AI. Using AI to draft captions, outline blog posts, generate ad copy variations, or research your audience is fully in line with Fiverr’s AI guidelines. Just make sure the final content is authentic and guided by your own professional judgment.
  • Using AI to create fake reviews, fabricate client testimonials, generate misleading visuals, produce deepfakes, or impersonate others violates Fiverr’s Community Standards and is not permitted anywhere, including in your external marketing.
  • No. Social media profiles, community participation, and a simple link-in-bio page are all effective alternatives.
  • Generally, organic channels are a better starting point. Paid advertising works best once you know who your ideal client is and have a well-reviewed profile.
  • Yes. Fiverr has freelancers specializing in social media, advertising, content writing, and web design who can help you build your off-platform presence.
  • Yes. A dedicated business account keeps your professional presence focused and allows you to tailor your content to your potential clients.

Repeat business score

As a freelancer on Fiverr, you know the importance of receiving repeat orders from your clients. Not only does repeat business confirm the high quality of your service (go you!) but also gives you peace of mind by helping you to create a stable income. Fiverr has always encouraged long-term relationships between clients and freelancers, and now, with the repeat business score and badge on freelancer profiles, this is recognized even further!

What does the repeat business score mean?

Your score gives you a sense of how well your repeat business compares to other freelancers within your subcategory. In this way, if you have Gigs in different subcategories, you’ll have a different repeat business score for each subcategory. Freelancers leading their subcategories, and who have a repeat business score of 95 and above, will earn the repeat business badge.

With the dashboard within the analytics tab, the metrics that make up the repeat business score are easily accessible.

Understand your repeat business performance based on the factors affecting your score:

  • The number of clients who ordered from you again within the last 90 days.
  • The percentage of clients who ordered from you again within the last 90 days.
  • Your earnings from repeat orders (before any added fees/ taxes).
  • The percentage of your earnings from repeat clients from your total earnings.

How it works

  • After logging in, navigate to the ‘Analytics’ tab.
  • To the right of the ‘Overview’ tab (which you already know), you’ll find the ‘Repeat business’ tab.
  • Alternatively, you can select ‘Repeat business’ from the dropdown menu under ‘Overview.’
  • Choose your subcategory from the dropdown menu.
  • See your repeat business score and how you perform in each of the factors that comprise it:
    • Repeat buyers
    • Repeat buyers (%)
    • Earnings from repeat buyers
    • Earnings from repeat buyers (%)
  • At the bottom of the page, you’ll find a banner with tips and tricks (See more tips) to help you meet (or even exceed!) your clients’ expectations.

How to improve your score

  • Follow client requirements to the detail
  • The more you know about what your clients want, the better you can meet (or exceed!) their expectations.
  • Keep your clients updated
  • Make your clients feel like you’ve got their back - be quick to respond and share updates on their orders.
  • Get early feedback on your work
  • Get a feel for what your clients are thinking and be flexible about making changes before the order is completed.
  • Tell clients what else you have to offer
  • Clients often need extra services delivered. Let them know how else you can add value to an ongoing order.
  • Offer Gig subscriptions
  • By gaining repeat orders using subscriptions, you can establish client trust and business security for yourself.

FAQs

  • Yes, only you can see your repeat business score on the repeat business dashboard within the analytics tab.
  • The score is updated once a week and is seen on the dashboard itself. It also lets you know when the new update will be. However, the factors (the number and percentage of repeat buyers as well as the revenue and the percentage of revenue from repeat buyers) update in real-time. This means that you can see your repeat buyers and earnings from repeat buyers within the last 90 days as it happens.
  • No, currently, in some sub-categories, this score doesn’t exist. In the subcategories where the score isn’t supported, you will be notified in the dashboard.
  • Don’t worry! The repeat business score is relative to the subcategory only. Your repeat business score will not be compared to every other Gig on Fiverr but only to other Gigs in your subcategory.
  • Whether you have had the same client for 25 years or 25 minutes, the time between each purchase makes no difference. A returning client is simply an individual who has previously purchased your service and is now requesting to do so once again. The client is defined as a repeat buyer after an order has been completed, and not only after an order was created.
  • In this instance, we take your vacation days into account. Your vacation days are viewed as “disregarded days.” For example, if you took 5 vacation days, your repeat business score will be calculated on the stats based on the last 95 days (90 repeat business days as per the standard + 5 vacation days).

Requirements and guidelines for your Gig

On Fiverr, the service you offer is called a Gig. Your Gig showcases your talent to potential clients and gives them the information they need before they place an order. A clear, complete Gig helps clients understand exactly what you deliver, so they can choose you with confidence and start orders with fewer questions. This article explains how many Gigs you can create, what belongs in each part of your Gig, and the media rules you need to follow.

Before you begin

You create and manage Gigs from your freelancer account, and the number of Gigs you can have depends on your level. Check the following before you build a Gig:

  • Required: a Gig description in English. You can add other languages as long as all the information also appears in English.
  • Required: an audio or video sample if your Gig is in the Music & Audio category. You cannot publish the Gig without one.
  • Required: permission to use every image, video, and audio file you upload.
  • Optional: a video, a PDF, and physical shipping, depending on the service you offer.

For more tips, see Creating a Gig and Guidelines for selecting Gig images.

How many Gigs you can create

When you become a freelancer on Fiverr, we recommend creating only one Gig at first and focusing your time and effort on that service. After your first Gig earns positive client feedback and multiple sales, consider creating more. We count every Gig status toward your limit except deleted Gigs and automation Gigs, such as Logo Maker and Consultation Gigs.

Level

Gigs allowed

New

4

Level 1

10

Level 2

10

Top Rated

Gig title guidelines

  • We help you start your title with I will… Complete the sentence with the service you want to provide.
  • Keep your Gig title short, clear, and to the point. Clients should recognize what you offer immediately.

Category & subcategory guidelines

  • Select the most appropriate category and subcategory for the service you offer.
  • If you are not sure, search for similar services on Fiverr to see how other freelancers categorize theirs.
  • We also recommend a category and subcategory based on your Gig title.

We reserve the right to move your Gig to a more relevant category or subcategory when needed.

Gig description guidelines

Your Gig description is your first chance to introduce yourself to potential clients. Be personable and approachable, and describe your service in plain terms so clients can decide to place an order.

Follow these guidelines:

  • Be clear about the purpose of your Gig and the specific service you provide.
  • When relevant, explain the methods you use to perform your service.
  • Highlight the value of your service.
  • Proofread your description before you publish it, and check for grammatical errors and typos.
  • Do not share your email address, phone number, or third-party messaging apps for the sole purpose of doing business off Fiverr.
  • If your service requires contact details or login credentials for an external site, mention this in the Gig requirements section.
  • You can share a link to your website or portfolio to showcase your experience and skills.
  • Keep your Gig aligned with Fiverr’s Community Standards.

If you share your personal contact information or lead clients to do business off Fiverr, we may remove your Gig from the marketplace. We may also permanently suspend accounts that violate this rule repeatedly.

Media guidelines

These guidelines apply to all images, videos, audio files, and other content you use, including reviews you upload with files.

  • Make sure you have the right to use your images for commercial purposes. For example, a stock image where the owner granted you permission.

  • If you use copyrighted images, we may remove your Gig.

  • You can add files up to 5 GB.

  • Never include personal contact information in your media.

  • In all Design categories, your images must be original.

  • In all other categories, make sure you have permission to upload the image.

    • Follow our Guidelines for selecting Gig images.
    • Use images that are clear, high resolution, and sized correctly. Avoid pixelated images.
    • You can upload up to three images that describe or relate to your Gig service.
    • You can add a watermark to both your delivery preview and your completed orders inside your Gig portfolio.

  • A video showcases your skills and services, and it can also introduce you and your work to clients.

    • Keep your video to 75 seconds or less.
    • Use an accepted video format: mp4 or AVI.
    • After you add a video, we create a thumbnail and show it in the marketplace. Select the thumbnail from the video you want to upload.

  • Never include personal contact information in your videos. If you use a sample from your portfolio, it can include a previous client’s information only when that client gave you explicit permission.

  • In the Music & Audio category, you need to upload an audio or video sample before you can publish your Gig.

    • Use a supported audio format: mp3 or MPEG.
    • Keep your audio file to three minutes and 30 seconds or less.
    • Keep the audio file size below 10 MB.

  • You can use PDFs to present reports, data, marketing strategies, website and mobile app designs, case studies, and visual work such as logos and illustrations.

    • Uploading a PDF is optional.
    • You can upload up to two PDF files to your Gig.

  • How to add a PDF to your Gig

    • Go to the Gig PDF area.
    • Drag a PDF into the area, or click Browse and select the PDF you want to upload.

  • For more details, see Adding PDFs to your Gig.

Shipping physical deliverables

Some services on Fiverr are delivered physically, such as arts and crafts and collectible items.

  • If your service includes physical shipping, select the shipping option in your Gig.
  • If you do not offer a physical product, do not select the shipping option, and do not request a shipping fee from your clients.

For the full rules, see “Shipping Physical Deliverables” in our Terms of Service.

Best practices

  • Start with one Gig and add more only after it earns positive feedback and multiple sales.
  • Write a title a client can understand at a glance.
  • Proofread your description before you publish, so typos do not undercut your offer.
  • Use original images in Design categories, and confirm your rights to any image you use in other categories.
  • Keep all contact details out of your Gig text, images, and videos.
  • Add a video and a PDF when they help clients see the quality of your work.

  • Your level sets your limit: four Gigs at New, 10 Gigs at Level 1 and Level 2, and 30 Gigs at Top Rated.
  • Yes. Every Gig status counts toward your limit except deleted Gigs and automation Gigs, such as Logo Maker and Consultation Gigs.

  • Yes. You can share a link that showcases your experience and skills. You cannot share your email address, phone number, website, or third-party messaging apps in order to move business off Fiverr.

  • We may remove your Gig from the marketplace.

Success score

The Success score metric evaluates each of your Gigs in key areas related to the order process and your relationship with clients. It evaluates your Gigs in six key areas, ensuring you maintain a consistent track record of quality service. These individual Gig scores are then used to determine your overall Success score.

What is the Success score?

  • What it does: It provides a comprehensive evaluation of your Gig performance based on client satisfaction, communication, and other key order metrics.
  • Why it’s useful: The score is designed to be stable and provides a more accurate reflection of your long-term performance, preventing a single order from having too much impact.
  • Who it’s for: All freelancers.

How is the success score calculated?

The overall Success core is determined by considering the individual scores of all your Gigs.

  • Evaluation timeframe: The calculation considers a longer time period which provides a more accurate reflection of your performance over time. This stable approach allows you more time to learn from mistakes without immediate consequences.
  • Gig weighting: Gigs with a higher number of orders carry more weight in the overall score. Additionally, higher-value and more recent orders may have a greater impact on the Gig score.
  • Transparency: Only you, the freelancer, can see your Success core. Clients only see your overall Level.

What are the Key areas in evaluation?

The individual Gig scores are determined by examining the order history in six key areas. Each key area includes various related data points, both quantitative (numerical data like statistics and scores) and qualitative (descriptive data like feedback and reviews).

  • Examines data points from reviews and other statistics reflecting client happiness with the overall order experience.
  • Best practices:
    • Understand needs: Ask questions to ensure a clear understanding of client requirements. Learn more on enhancing order requirements.
    • Maintain communication: Regularly update clients on progress and address any concerns.
    • Exceed expectations: Deliver more value than expected to leave a lasting positive impression.
  • Determined by your responsiveness, helpfulness, and ability to set clear expectations.
  • Best practices:
    • Be professional: Use clear, respectful language and avoid jargon.
    • Prompt responses: Answer client inquiries quickly to show you value their time.
    • Set expectations: Outline your workflow and timelines to manage client expectations.
    • Provide updates: Keep clients informed about project status and any issues.
  • Tracks how often disputes and issues arise during the order process.
  • Best practices:
    • Set clear expectations: Clearly define your services and limitations on your Gig page.
    • Respect client concerns: Approach client concerns with empathy and offer solutions.
    • Maintain positive and polite communication: Keep interactions with clients polite and professional, ensuring a positive experience.
  • Learn more on understanding conflict free orders.
  • Examines the effect of cancellations on the overall order process.
  • Best practices:
    • Proactive communication: Address potential issues early to prevent cancellations.
    • Understand needs: Clarify client requirements to avoid misunderstandings.
    • Offer alternative solutions: When issues or concerns arise, provide alternative options to help resolve the situation and avoid cancellations.
  • Still, there are moments when completing the order isn’t the best path forward. Knowing when to cancel, and how to do it thoughtfully, can protect your reputation and your client’s experience.
  • Learn how to decide when walking away from an order is the right move by reading “To cancel or not to cancel” in the community forum.
  • Reflects how often you deliver on time or ahead of time, factoring in the frequency of late deliveries.
  • Best practices:
    • Meet deadlines: Stick to agreed timelines or deliver early if possible.
    • Manage expectations: Set realistic deadlines and keep clients informed of any changes.
  • Shows if clients feel they received the value they paid for.
  • Best practices:
    • Clear pricing: Ensure clients understand your pricing and what it includes.
    • Deliver quality: Provide high-quality work that meets or exceeds expectations.

See more tips for best practices here.

What if my score drops or is not increasing?

Success scores can drop due to various factors, including:

  • Negative Reviews: Receiving lower ratings or negative feedback from clients can impact your score.
  • Late Deliveries: Consistently delivering orders late can reduce your score.
  • Order Cancellations: High rates of order cancellations, especially if initiated by you, can negatively affect your score.
  • Poor Communication: Ineffective or slow communication with clients can lead to a lower score.
  • Conflicts: Frequent disputes or conflicts with clients during the order process can also contribute to a drop in your Success score.
  • Decreased Client Satisfaction: If clients feel that the value of your service does not meet their expectations, it can result in a lower score.

If your score is not increasing, focus on continuous improvement and delivering quality service.

We understand that there are edge cases and exceptions. The following actions will not impact your score:

  • Unresponsive Clients: Unresponsive clients do not negatively impact your Success score. The leveling system accounts for these scenarios.
  • Enhancing the client experience: Actions such as revisions, delivery extensions, or partial refunds are evaluated based on their impact on overall client satisfaction. They are viewed as tools to enhance the client’s experience.

If your Success score falls critically low, your account may be labeled low performance, which will affect your visibility. Focus on the best practices above to improve.

FAQs

  • You can view the details of your Success score on your level overview page. Expand each Gig score under Scores by Gig to see which key areas have the strongest impact, both positively and negatively.
  • The Success score is based on your performance relative to other freelancers in your price range. A score of 10 is not required for success. Interested in learning strategic tips from CSMs, don’t overlook this key factor in your Success score.
  • The Success Score may be impacted by extended periods of inactivity or a lack of active orders.
  • Meeting a certain Success score alone isn’t enough to reach a higher level, you must meet all other criteria (ratings, orders, unique clients, earnings). You can learn more about Fiverr’s Level System.

Top Rated freelancers

The Top Rated level lets clients know which freelancers have been recognized for the highest level of quality and service. Our level system is designed to offer you more transparency, actionable insights, and a clear view of your progress.

Learn more about the benefits of Fiverr’s level system.

How do I qualify for a Top Rated review?

All Top Rated freelancers are individually reviewed and approved by Fiverr’s evaluation team.

To qualify for this review, you must first meet the following criteria.

Some categories require additional prerequisites or mandatory skill tests before you can progress to a review.

What happens after I qualify?

Once you meet the criteria, the evaluation team reviews your eligibility for Top Rated status. The team currently focuses on high-demand categories that are in need of more Top Rated freelancers.

After the review, you receive an email with the team’s decision.

  • If you are approved: You see your new Top Rated status on your dashboard and your level overview page.
  • If you are not approved: You receive an email with the primary reason for the decision. You stay at Level 2, and if your metrics still qualify in six months, you are eligible for another review.

How does the Top Rated review work?

The evaluation team performs a holistic review, examining four key areas when considering your eligibility for Top Rated status.

Fiverr’s 4 evaluation pillars:
  • This pillar measures your ability to deliver high-quality work that aligns with your service descriptions and the client’s expectations.
  • What the team looks for:
    • Proficiency and Quality: The actual quality of your final deliverables in relation to the scope and complexity of the services you provide.
    • Skill Alignment: Ensuring your work demonstrates the specific professional skills you advertise on your profile and Gigs.
  • A smooth and professional client experience is essential. This pillar evaluates how effectively you manage client interactions from the initial message to final delivery.
  • What the team looks for:
    • Responsiveness: Your overall response rate and ability to reply to client inquiries promptly.
    • Expectation Setting: Your skill in setting clear expectations regarding delivery timelines, scope of work, and revisions to avoid misunderstandings.
    • Seamless Experience: Providing consistently smooth service that makes the client feel valued and informed throughout the process.
  • This pillar assesses how you present yourself and your services on the platform, ensuring you are easy to find, understand, and trustworthy.
  • What the team looks for:
    • Gig and profile structure: The clarity, organization, and completeness of your Gigs and freelancer profile. Your descriptions should be well-written and accurately reflect your offerings.
    • Feature utilization: Effective use of platform features, such as:
      • An intro video to personally connect with prospective clients.
      • A portfolio to clearly showcase your best work, skills, and experience.
  • This is a non-negotiable pillar that ensures a safe and trustworthy marketplace for everyone.
  • What the team looks for:
    • Terms of Service adherence: Verification that all your account activity and conversations comply with our Terms of Service.
    • Community standards: Confirmation that your content and behavior adhere to the Community standards, maintaining a professional environment.

Best practices: Dos & Don’ts

We recommend you follow these Dos and Don’ts to support your eligibility:

Dos ✅
Don’ts ❌

Present yourself professionally.

Build an attractive and trustworthy presence on Fiverr with exceptional Gig pages and a freelancer profile.

Misrepresent yourself or your business.

Clearly represent your qualifications, services, and identity. Refrain from unauthorized use of content or deceptive pricing in all aspects of your Gig offerings.

Deliver exceptional value.

Ensure every service you offer provides outstanding value in terms of price, timeliness, and expertise. Demonstrate flexibility to customize your work according to the buyer’s specific needs.

Duplicate any active Gigs or services.

Ensure your Gigs offer different services and are not synonymous with each other.

Make sure to meet client expectations.

Provide services that match your Gig’s description and requirements.

Don’t violate our Terms of Service or Community Standards.

Your participation in the level system is determined by your content and behavior on the platform.

How do I maintain Top Rated status?

As a Top Rated freelancer, you must maintain the required metrics to keep your status.

If any of your metrics fall below the minimum requirements, you enter a 30-day grace period.

  • If you improve your metrics during that time, you keep your Top Rated status.
  • If you are unable to improve, the evaluation team reviews your account to determine whether or not you can remain Top Rated. Your Top Rated status prevents you from being automatically moved to a lower level.

If the team decides you should move to a lower level, you can be evaluated again after a six-month waiting period if your metrics still qualify.

Your level may change at any time due to periodic evaluations and may not always be subject to a 30-day grace period.

What’s the timeline for the review and category openings?

Our review process ensures that each qualified freelancer receives the attention they deserve.

The evaluation team prioritizes reviews for high-demand categories that need more Top Rated freelancers, where those freelancers can benefit from more business. If your Gigs are not in one of the categories listed below, we are unable to estimate a time frame for your review.

Please note: Simply adding a Gig to a listed category will not give you access to a prioritized review. You must have at least 20 completed orders in one of the listed categories to be eligible.

Note: Seller Plus Premium members have priority in the evaluation queue. Learn more about Seller Plus Premium.

Understanding Fiverr’s freelancer levels

The Fiverr level system is designed to reward you for providing exceptional service and growing your business. As you progress, you unlock benefits and tools that guide you toward continuous improvement, helping you reach your full potential on Fiverr.

About Fiverr’s level system

The level system is a program that recognizes your experience and performance on the platform.

  • What it does: It tracks your progress across key metrics and automatically assigns you a level.
  • Why it’s useful: Advancing levels can increase your chances of getting orders and gives you access to beneficial features.
  • Who it’s for: All freelancers on Fiverr. Your level is visible to clients on Gig cards, Gig pages, and your freelancer profile.
Accessing your level overview

The Level Overview page gives you a view of your progress and shows how close you are to qualifying for the next level.

You can access it in two ways:

  • Log in to your account and click on your level displayed on the top left of your dashboard.
  • Navigate through the top header menu by going to “Growth & Marketing” and then clicking on “Level Overview”.
Level criteria & metrics

Your level is determined by your performance across six key metrics and certain criteria.

Performance Metrics
  • This analyzes your Gigs in key areas related to the order process and your relationship with clients, relative to other freelancers. Your overall Success Score is determined by the individual scores of each Gig. Learn more about the Success score.
  • This reflects the average of all ratings provided by clients you have worked with over the past two years. The rating displayed on your profile, however, reflects your all-time ratings. Learn more with Reviews and ratings for freelancers.
  • This shows how often you replied to new messages within 24 hours over the last 90 days. Learn more with Best practices for Fiverr freelancers.
  • This shows the total number of orders you have completed on Fiverr.

Progress tracker & leveling

The progress tracker provides an at-a-glance view of your journey in the level system and allows you to see how close you are to qualifying for the next level.

  • To move up to Level 1 or Level 2, you must meet the criteria in all six metrics. Once you qualify, you’ll move up automatically within 24 hours. To progress to Top Rated, you will also need to pass a manual evaluation to confirm your eligibility.
  • If your performance drops below the criteria for your current level, you will enter a 30-day grace period.
    • For Level 1 or Level 2 freelancers: If you cannot improve your stats during the grace period, you will move down to the level that corresponds with your current metrics.
    • For Top Rated freelancers: If you cannot improve your stats during the grace period, your account will be reviewed to determine if you can remain Top Rated or need to move to a lower level.
    • If your metrics fall below the criteria for Level 1, you will move to Level 0.
    • If your Success Score drops to a critically low level, your account will be labeled low performance, and your visibility on the platform will be affected.

Your level may change at any time due to periodic evaluations.
